title: Applied AI Product Manager
description:
Summary
 Position Summary 
Applied AI Product Manager
Overview
Job Description
An Applied AI Product Manager is a senior individual contributor responsible for ensuring a product’s value and viability within a product line. This role involves leading empowered, cross-functional product teams to solve moderate complexity customer problems that align with high value business needs. The Applied AI Product Manager is accountable for the product’s success, from vision to execution, and collaborates closely with various functions and stakeholders to deliver valuable, viable, usable, and feasible solutions. The Applied AI Product Manager harnesses AI and agentic tools to compress the concept-to-cash learning loop—automating analysis, prototyping, and compliance detail-work so the team can focus on the human judgment AI cannot replace: product sense-making.
Key Responsibilities
• Product Accountability
• Responsible and accountable for the product's value and viability showcasing a measurable Return on Investments (ROI)
• Drive strategy-aligned solutions to achieve product value objectives.
• Formulate and achieve Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for identified problems to solve.
• Measure KPIs and analyze outcomes to inform future strategies.
• Leverage AI to harvest outcome evidence early and often, lowering total cost of ownership (TCO).
• Vision and Strategy
• Co-create, own, and evangelize the product vision, strategy, and roadmap, using AI to deepen domain knowledge and simulate future scenarios to chart pathways others have not yet seen.
• Align product objectives with the product line and business goals.
• Co-create in collaboration with business stakeholders, engineering, experience, and delivery.
• Use AI to expedite research, gather evidence, bolster domain knowledge, and craft and innovative visions backed by compelling strategic rationale. 
• Market and User Engagement
• Conduct user research and competitive analysis, using AI agents to synthesize research at speed—accelerating the data crunching, ensuring the human connection.
• Engage the team with users and stakeholders through continuous research and direct interactions.
• Collaborate and guide the team toward solutions that address priority user and business needs.
• Apply analytical skills to analyze data and derive actionable insights, shifting from waiting on analysis to working on insights.
• Adopt innovative and experimental approaches to solving complex problems, including AI-built, disposable prototypes that validate solutions quickly and retire bad ideas just as fast.
• Collaboration and Teamwork
• Work side-by-side with cross-functional (business, engineering, experience, and delivery) team members to achieve KPI outcomes.
• Promote a product operating model that emphasizes outcomes over output (minimize overproduction while maximizing value).
• Build empowered teams and product communities who exhibit collective product ownership and level-up their outcome potential through AI and agentic tools.
• Continuous Improvement 
• Promote and drive rapid, emergent, and ongoing learning and adaptation to meet objectives.
• Drive innovation and improvement of the process to drive out waste and accelerate value achievement, using AI as a force-multiplier to offload the repetitive, speed up the sluggish, and automate the mundane.
• Remove obstacles for the team and ensure smooth flow of continuous value achievement. 
• Spread knowledge and best practices within the product vertical community.
• Applied AI Ways of Working
• Amplify innovation: use AI to rapidly deepen domain knowledge, surface untapped market and user potential, and simulate future scenarios—charting new pathways for the business.
• Amplify learning: use AI agents to synthesize research and validate ideas before they enter the backlog—compressing lead time by accelerating the data crunching, ensuring the human connection.
• Amplify focus: act as Editor-in-Chief—using AI to rigorously test assumptions and retire ideas that do not genuinely serve the user’s workflow in a way that works for the business.
• Amplify experimentation: use AI to build early, functional, disposable prototypes that validate the architecture and the solution, playing a key role in the Agentic Secure Software Development Life Cycle that paves a clear path to productionize early and often.
Required Qualifications
• Education: Bachelor’s degree in business, Marketing, Engineering, or a related field. 
• 10+ years of proven experience in lean product management or related roles.
• 3+ years enterprise scale experience across multiple business areas. 
• 1+ years of building AI based intelligent products 
• 1+ year’s experience in using GenAI tools to perform product management tasks like conduct idea research, shaping, synthesis, roadmaps, requirements, prototyping, testing
Preferred Qualifications
• Preferred Education: An MBA or related advanced degree is preferred.
• Preferred Experience:
• Demonstrated experience in modern product craft of delivering the right thing, in the right way, at the right time. Significant experience in lean product management craft and domain (tools, methods, and practices). Seen as a leader in this space. 
• Proven accountability for value, viability and P&L objectives for a product and for an empowered product team. 
• Preferred Skills 
• Communication: Clear and effective communication with team members, stakeholders, and customers. Excellent communication and collaboration abilities. 
• Leadership: Ability to lead and inspire cross-functional teams, fostering collaboration and collective movement toward product goals. Ability to influence at all organizational levels through inclusion and leadership.
• Customer-Centricity: Deep understanding of customer needs and engagement patterns, driving teams to deliver solutions that customers love and that work for the business. Expertise in applying customer-centric methods and practices.
• Strategic Thinking: Ability to develop and execute a strategic vision for the product, aligning it with broader business objectives.
• Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills. 
• Detail-oriented, organized, and visionary.
• Learning-forward, experimental, and value-oriented mindset.
• Ability to navigate complexity and uncertainty. 
• Quick to reach expert-level knowledge within the product domain being served. 
• AI Agentic Fluency: Comfortable orchestrating multiple AI agents across the concept-to-cash flow (research, insight, prototyping, specification, coding, and compliance), with guardrails at each hand-off—assumptions, confidence levels, and links to sources of truth.
• AI Realism and Eval Fluency: Understands the difference between deterministic logic and probabilistic generation; designs guardrails for hallucination, bias, and drift; uses evaluation harnesses before launch and monitors drift after, with a kill-switch mentality—and knows when not to use AI.
• Experience with modern agentic AI tools such as Claude Code, Claude Co-work, Open AI Codex Cursor, and Visual Studio Code.
• Preferred Personal Traits 
• Strong leadership capabilities.
• Customer-centric mindset.
• Ability to work as an individual contributor in a collaborative, cross-functional team.
• Humble, curious, and learning-forward mindset.
• Favor small step action and evidence over detailed upfront planning and precision aiming.
• Experience with lean solutions and rapid, inexpensive experimentation to emerge the right thing, in the right way, at the right time.
• High levels of continuous customer and user engagement.
• Treats taste and judgment as the un-automatable moat—using AI to amplify, never replace, product sense-making.
Conclusion
The Applied AI Product Manager plays a crucial role in ensuring the success of our high value, moderately complex products by balancing customer needs with business objectives. This role requires a blend of strategic vision, analytical skills, and collaborative teamwork to deliver valuable, viable, usable, and feasible solutions. It demands significant experience in the modern product management craft and a drive for continuous improvement—amplified by the fluent, responsible use of AI to learn faster and earn faster.

Bright is a profitable, India-built, U.S.-market Consumer FinTech, with revenue trajectory to $100M in the coming 6 months. The business model combines subscription revenue with a financial service marketplace revenues, for loans, credit cards, and credit building tools.
Bright has launched an AI money assistant and AI agentic UX flows for access to credit. It will be the first AI-driven Consumer FinTech for middle-income consumers.
The Bright product suite has potential for global markets beyond the US. The market size is 100M global middle-income consumers, with a revenue pool opportunity of $15B.

You will work closely with engineering, AI/ML, design, architecture, presales, and business teams to translate customer needs into scalable AI product capabilities.

title: Staff, AI Product Management (Global Functions)
description:
About the Role:
GSK’s Enterprise AI team, a highly skilled applied AI group, translates the promise of AI into measurable impact across every major group at GSK — R&D, Medical, Commercial, Supply Chain, HR, Legal, Finance, and beyond. Bionic pods — AI product managers, forward deployed engineers, full-stack engineers, data engineers, and digital workers — embed directly with scientific and business teams to build AI products that change outcomes.
We are hiring a Staff, AI Product Manager (Director level equivalent role) to own a major slice of our Global Functions portfolio and act as the strategic counterpart to the engineers and digital workers in your pod, setting the forward deployed strategy they execute against. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who can identify and shape high-value AI opportunities across the key areas of Global Functions - HR, Legal, Compliance, Procurement, or Finance, build the case to fund and deploy against them, and ensure FDEs are working on what matters most. You will not manage engineers; you will shape what they build in your domain and how we measure whether it worked.
Why This Role Exists:
Forward deployed teams are most powerful when paired with sharp opportunity selection. Enterprise AI has no separate strategy layer: the AI Product Manager sets the forward deployed strategy, and the pod executes it. This role closes that gap at this level by ensuring the engineers we deploy are working on the right things.
In this role you will be the person who:
• Owns a clear domain or capability area within the Enterprise AI opportunity portfolio.
• Identifies, sizes, and shapes the highest-value AI opportunities in that domain.
• Partners daily with forward deployed, full-stack, and data engineering leads to scope and steer engagements end-to-end.
• Builds the business and executive alignment the pod needs to land and scale.
How This Differs from Traditional Product Management:
This is not a traditional enterprise product role managing a source system’s roadmap, releases, and backlog. As an AI Product Manager in Enterprise AI, you:
• Build new AI products from ambiguous, unsolved business problems rather than evolving an established platform.
• Work with probabilistic systems — defining evaluations, acceptable error, and human oversight instead of fixed functional requirements.
• Help lead a bionic pod, deciding which work goes to engineers and which to digital workers, and how they hand off.
• Prototype hands on and are measured on business outcomes, not features shipped or system uptime.
Key Responsibilities:
Opportunity Identification & Value Sizing:
• Hunt for high-value AI opportunities within your assigned domain at GSK; develop a structured pipeline of opportunities ranked by impact, feasibility, and time-to-value.
• Quantify value rigorously. Build credible business cases that survive finance and senior business unit scrutiny — cycle time saved, decisions accelerated, revenue uplift, cost avoided, scientific productivity gained.
• Develop deep domain pattern recognition so you can spot AI-shaped problems in workflows the business itself hasn’t yet articulated.
Strategic Prioritization & Portfolio Shaping:
• Shape the opportunity portfolio in your domain. Maintain a living view of in-flight, queued, and de-prioritized opportunities, with the rationale for each decision, and feed it into the broader Enterprise AI portfolio.
• Make trade-off recommendations. When two business sponsors both want an FDE pod, defines the success metrics, run the analysis and recommend where engineers go.
• Protect engineering focus. Push back — with evidence — on opportunities that won’t move scalable outcomes. 
Engineering Partnership & Enablement
• Be the strategic counterpart to forward deployed, full-stack, and data engineering leads in your domain. Translate ambiguous business problems into crisp problem statements, prototypes, success metrics, and decision frameworks engineers can build against.
• Shape engagements end-to-end. Define scope, success criteria, exit conditions, and scaling pathways before kick-off, then stay close as engineers execute.
• Surface re-use and platform leverage when a one-off solution should become a reusable capability.
• Design the human–digital split. Decide which tasks the pod’s digital workers own, where engineers and business users stay in the loop, and how evaluation and oversight make that safe.
Stakeholder Alignment & Communication
• Operate fluently with VP-level business and scientific leaders. Run conversations that turn fuzzy ambitions into concrete, fundable AI engagements.
• Build sponsor coalitions that secure data access, change-management commitment, and air cover for your engagements.
• Communicate impact clearly in language that connects AI work to patients, science, and enterprise outcomes.
Measurement, Learning & Iteration
• Apply Enterprise AI’s value-realization framework to every engagement in your domain and improve it with what you learn.
• Run honest post-mortems and feed lessons back into how your domain selects opportunities.
Required Functional Experience:
• 18+ years of progressive experience spanning some combination of pharma/life sciences, AI/ML product strategy, and senior product management or strategy roles in technology-led organisations.
• Demonstrated track record of identifying, scoping, prototyping, and shepherding high-value technology or AI initiatives from problem framing through funding into delivery.
• Strong working knowledge of at least one part of the pharma value chain — R&D, clinical, medical, manufacturing, commercial, or an enterprise function — including the data, decisions, and constraints inside it.
• Solid technical fluency in modern AI/ML — LLMs, agentic systems, and digital workers, ML lifecycle, data and evaluation patterns — sufficient to leverage evidence from rapid prototyping to challenge engineers, scope realistically, and avoid hype-driven choices.
• Experience operating as a senior individual contributor — leading through influence, frameworks, and quality of thinking rather than headcount.
• A product management or product-strategy heritage: discovery, opportunity sizing, roadmap shaping, prototyping, and stakeholder alignment — ideally on products whose core behaviour is AI rather than conventional software.
#AGTech
Skills
AI Platforms, AI Product Management, Generative AI, Machine Learning (ML), Production Strategy, Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), Product Roadmap, Statistical Analysis, User Needs Analysis
Why GSK?
Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.
GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.
People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people.

title: Product Manager - Clinical Data Science & GenAI
description:

Position Summary: We’re looking for a Product Manager in Bangalore to help shape the future of athenahealth’s AI-Native Electronic Health Record. The Product Manager will lead the Clinical Data Science product area, developing the machine learning, generative AI, and evaluation capabilities that power clinical AI experiences.
About the Team: The Clinical Foundations team builds shared capabilities that support athenahealth’s electronic health record products. Team members partner with Product, Engineering, Design, Data Science, Clinical Informaticists, and Patient Safety professionals to deliver scalable, enterprise-grade AI product features.
The Team
• Integrates frontier lab large language models. 
• Builds in-house machine learning models. 
• Uses AI evaluation and observability platforms such as Arize, Kubeflow, and DataDog. 
• Uses Responsible AI practices to build solutions with the safety and efficacy required in a healthcare setting. 
• Develops AI capabilities that help reduce cognitive and administrative burdens in healthcare and ultimately improve patient outcomes. 
Essential Job Responsibilities
• Define the product vision, business cases, and roadmap for the Clinical Data Science product area. 
• Serve as Product Owner for assigned Scrum teams by defining epics and user stories, prioritizing the backlog, and making informed trade-offs across customer value, scope, timing, and technical constraints. 
• Define the end-to-end product development lifecycle, including problem definition, requirements, user experience, objectives and key results, delivery, and measurement of customer and business outcomes. 
• Establish and monitor performance measures that provide visibility into product outcomes, risks, and opportunities for improvement. 
• Partner with Product, Engineering, Design, Data Science, Patient Safety, Legal, and business leaders to align product decisions with healthcare safety, regulatory, and operational needs. 
• Evaluate market conditions, customer needs, product dependencies, and business value to guide prioritization and product investment decisions. 
• Collaborate with Sales, Customer Success, and Product Marketing to develop clear customer-facing product information and service descriptions. 
• Support product teams in applying shared AI evaluation tools and governance practices across their business areas. 
• Share product management and responsible AI practices through coaching, documentation, and working sessions. 
• Contribute to planning and coordination across the broader Product Management organization. 
• Partner with product leadership to define use-case-specific evaluation strategies, benchmarks, success metrics, acceptance thresholds, and release criteria for generative AI capabilities. 
Expected Education & Experience
• Bachelor’s degree required; a degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Business, or a related field is preferred. 
• Minimum 8+ years of Product Management or related experience. 
• Experience in healthcare or healthcare technology is preferred. 
• Practical experience developing generative AI solutions using large language models (LLMs), including prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), model APIs, and analysis of model outputs. 
• Experience with LLM evaluation methods, including deterministic evaluations, LLM-as-Judge, subject matter expert annotation workflows, and online evaluations. 
• Experience with AI evaluation and observability platforms, such as Arize, Datadog, LangSmith, or Braintrust. 
• Experience designing or managing responsible AI solutions in regulated or high-impact environments, including safety testing, hallucination risk management, bias evaluation, auditability, data lineage, and compliance. 
• Knowledge of modern AI systems and practices, including large language models, RAG architecture, AI agents, observability, evaluation pipelines, model governance, prompt engineering, explainability, traceability, and production AI operations. 
• Experience working with Agile or Scrum product development teams. 
• Ability to analyze complex problems, use qualitative and quantitative evidence, and develop scalable product solutions. 
• Experience using AI tools such as Claude, Copilot, ChatGPT, and Figma Make to accelerate product development, including drafting requirements, synthesizing user feedback, creating specifications or prototypes, and analyzing data with appropriate human review.

We are a diverse group of dreamers and do-ers with unique knowledge, expertise, backgrounds, and perspectives. We unite as mission-driven problem-solvers with a deep desire to achieve our vision and make our time here count. title: Senior Product Manager (AI)
description:
We are building Atlas, Pepper's agentic operating system, and we want a Senior Product Manager who loves mar-tech to own a core surface of it and ship fast.
About Pepper
Pepper is the Agentic Organic Growth System that drives outcomes. Today's fastest-growing companies trust Pepper to drive growth via SEO and AI-search, combining strategy, AI agents, and embedded expert operators. We drive content-led growth for 2,500+ industry leaders, including Amazon, Google, Unilever, Atlassian, HSBC, Instacart, ITC, and Xiaomi.
We are organic growth infrastructure for the AI era. AI search rewrote the rules of discovery, SEO tools did not catch up, and agencies did not reskill. Pepper was built for this new layer, where strategy, agents, and operators work as one system, and where we own outcomes rather than just dashboards or deliverables. Atlas is the agentic operating system that powers it all.
About the role
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to own a meaningful surface of Atlas, driving it from discovery through launch and iteration inside a fast-paced, customer-obsessed organization.
You should be genuinely excited about mar-tech and the marketing ecosystems that teams work in. The best person for this role finds the marketing stack interesting in its own right: how marketers plan, create, optimize, and measure, and how an agentic system can change all of it. You will be building product for marketers and growth teams, so understanding their world deeply matters.
This role rewards both depth and speed. The ambition is long-term and transformational, but the cadence is fast. We want someone who thinks sharply, ships quickly, and iterates in tight loops.
It also involves real change management. You will work closely with our services teams and their operational workflows, encoding how expert work actually gets done into product. Comfort with Service as a Software thinking, where software and agents transform how a service is delivered, is a strong plus.
This role is based out of Pepper's Mumbai office in Andheri East and is on-site.
What you will own
• Own a core surface of Atlas end to end, from discovery and definition through launch and iteration.
• Write crisp product specs that identify the problem, set goals, and define success metrics so design and engineering can build with clarity.
• Run product discovery: talk to customers, study usage data, and turn what you learn into a sharp, prioritized roadmap.
• Build AI workflows, agents, and automations that make expert marketing and SEO work repeatable.
• Partner with services teams to translate real operational workflows into scalable product.
• Ship, measure, and iterate, with a steady diet of product usage data informing every next move.
• Work hand in hand with engineering, design, data science, and customer success to deliver outcomes, not just features.
What you bring to the table
• You have built B2B products. You have several years of product management experience, typically five or more, with real depth shipping B2B software.
• You have worked with US customers. You have built for and worked closely with US customers, and you understand how enterprise buyers and marketing teams there evaluate, adopt, and expect to be supported.
• You are excited about mar-tech. You find marketing technology and the marketing ecosystem genuinely interesting, and you want to build the tools that marketers and growth teams rely on.
• You move fast and think sharply. You ship quickly, iterate in tight loops, and stay scrappy when the situation calls for it.
• You are technical enough. You are comfortable with APIs, authentication, and integrations, and you can hold your own in technical discussions with engineering.
• You are strong on product craft. You write clearly, deconstruct complex problems, take a data-driven approach, and have sound judgment on when to iterate, discard, or scale.
• You work shoulder to shoulder. You are at home with engineering, design, data science, and customer success, and you build real relationships with customers and stakeholders.
Why this role matters
This is not a role managing a backlog at the edge of a finished product. You will own a real surface of Atlas and shape how marketing teams plan, execute, and measure organic growth in the AI era, with the speed of a startup and a customer base of 2,500+ brands already counting on Pepper.
If you love mar-tech, have built B2B products, and want to build for US customers who will actually use what you ship, this is the seat.
Location: On-site, Pepper, Mumbai (Andheri East). This is a long-term role.

As a Senior Product Manager for AI Data Products, you will own the product vision and roadmap for building the semantic layer, ontology frameworks, and knowledge mapping systems that enable AI agents to operate effectively across supply chain workflows.
You will define how business concepts such as demand signals, forecast overrides, promotional lifts, safety stock policies, perpetual inventory adjustments, and replenishment constraints are modeled, connected, and exposed to AI systems in a structured, explainable, and scalable way.
This role requires a unique blend of:
• Product leadership
• Data architecture fluency
• AI/ML platform understanding
• Supply chain domain depth
• Strong stakeholder influence across global teams

Build Explain ability & Trust Frameworks: 
• Establish product capabilities that surface contextual reasoning, lineage, and governance controls so AI-generated insights are transparent, auditable, and trusted by planners and buyers.
Drive Strategic Road mapping & Execution: 
• Own a multi-quarter roadmap for semantic and knowledge capabilities, defining clear requirements and delivering incremental value through structured releases aligned to supply chain priorities.
Lead Cross-Functional Alignment: 
• Partner across Supply Chain, Product, Engineering, and Architecture teams globally to align business definitions, resolve ambiguity, and accelerate adoption of AI-powered decision platforms.

Required:
• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, or related field.

• Semantic layers, ontologies, or knowledge graphs
• Data modeling and metadata management
• API-based data access layers
• Strong SQL and data analytics fluency.
• Experience partnering closely with Data Science and Engineering teams.
• Experience operating in complex, ambiguous enterprise environments.
Highly Desirable:

• Experience with Blue Yonder (JDA), ERP, or retail replenishment systems.
• Exposure to LLM-powered systems or agent frameworks.
• Experience building explainable AI systems.

Additional Skills:

Nice-to-have

• Experience with enterprise sales cycles, RFPs or tenders.
• Products shipped into banking, government or other regulated industries.
How to apply

• Ensure your resume includes a link to something you built mostly with coding agents (a repo, a live URL or a 3-minute Loom).
• Ensure your resume includes a short paragraph on one thing the agent got wrong and how you caught it.

title: Staff, AI Product Manager
description:
About the Role:
GSK’s Enterprise AI team, a highly skilled applied AI group, translates the promise of AI into measurable impact across every major group at GSK — R&D, Medical, Commercial, Supply Chain, HR, Legal, Finance, and beyond. Bionic pods — AI product managers, forward deployed engineers, full-stack engineers, data engineers, and AI agents and workers — embed directly with scientific and business teams to build AI products that change outcomes.
We are hiring a Staff, AI Product Manager to own Emerging Tech and AI Tooling, the front edge of GSK’s AI platform estate. You will run structured evaluation of new AI tools and platforms, decide what graduates into a standing tower and what gets retired, and own the AI developer tooling GSK engineers use every day. It suits someone who can hold an evaluation to a decision date and retire tools the organisation is attached to. You will lead a small engineering squad and set direction a far larger estate inherits.
Why This Role Exists:
Every week brings a new AI tool and a stakeholder who wants it. Without a disciplined front door, evaluations never close and nothing is ever retired. This role runs that front door, and owns the developer tooling estate so the tools engineers depend on daily have a named owner rather than a shared inbox.
In this role you will be the person who:
• Owns the evaluation portfolio for new AI tools and platforms across Enterprise AI.
• Decides what graduates into a standing platform tower, what holds, and what gets retired.
• Owns the AI developer tooling estate end to end.
• Hands graduated platforms over with a working operating model.
How This Differs from Traditional Product Management:
This is not a traditional enterprise product role managing a source system’s roadmap, releases, and backlog. As an AI Product Manager in Enterprise AI, you:
• Build new AI products from ambiguous, unsolved business problems.
• Work with probabilistic systems, defining evaluations, acceptable error, and human oversight.
• Help lead a bionic pod, deciding which work goes to engineers and which to AI agents and workers, and how they hand off.
• Prototype hands on and are measured on business outcomes.
Key Responsibilities: 
Evaluation & Graduation:
• Run every evaluation to a decision. Set the hypothesis, the success bar, the comparison set, and the kill date up front. Keep a live view of what is in flight, on hold, or retired.
• Quantify value rigorously. Build credible adoption and retirement cases that survive finance and architecture scrutiny — engineering hours saved, licence cost avoided, capability gained, duplication removed.
• Tell new capability from repackaging so overlap with what GSK already runs is caught before it becomes duplicate spend.
Strategic Prioritization & Portfolio Shaping:
• Shape the emerging tech portfolio. Keep a living view of in-flight, queued, and retired evaluations with the rationale for each call, and feed it into the AI Platforms & Tools portfolio.
• Make the graduate, retire, or hold call. Decide which tower receives a graduating platform, and hold the decision date when the organisation would rather extend it.
• Protect the estate from sprawl. Say no, with evidence, to tools that look attractive but do not change what the organisation can actually do.
Engineering Partnership & Enablement:
• Lead the Emerging Tech and AI Tooling squad. Set direction for a small full-stack team across evaluation builds and the tooling estate, and stay close enough to review the work.
• Own the graduation handover. Hand the receiving tower an operating model, support path, and entitlement design.
• Own the AI developer tooling estate. Run access, entitlement, support, and adoption for the coding and desktop tools engineers depend on daily.
• Stay hands on. Prototype alongside the team and form your own judgment on a tool by using it.
Stakeholder Alignment & Communication:
• Operate fluently with VP-level technology and business leaders. Run conversations that turn vendor enthusiasm into a testable hypothesis with a decision date.
• Build sponsor coalitions that secure evaluation funding, pilot cohorts, and the air cover to retire tools people are attached to.
• Communicate impact clearly in language that connects tooling investment to engineering throughput and enterprise outcomes.
Measurement, Learning & Iteration:
• Apply Enterprise AI’s value-realization framework to every evaluation and graduation and improve it with what you learn.
• Run honest post-mortems on evaluations that failed, and feed lessons back into how the front door selects what to test. 
Required skills:
• 16+ years of progressive experience spanning some combination of pharma/life sciences, AI/ML product strategy, and senior product management or strategy roles in technology-led organisations.
• Demonstrated track record of identifying, scoping, prototyping, and shepherding high-value technology or AI initiatives from problem framing through funding into delivery.
• Strong working knowledge of enterprise AI platforms and developer tooling — how they are licensed, entitled, supported, and adopted at scale — and of at least one part of the pharma value chain.
• Solid technical fluency in modern AI/ML — LLMs, agentic systems, AI agents and workers, ML lifecycle, data and evaluation patterns — sufficient to leverage evidence from rapid prototyping to challenge engineers, scope realistically, and avoid hype-driven choices.
• Experience leading a small engineering team while operating with a span of influence far wider than the headcount — leading through frameworks, evidence, and quality of thinking.
• A product management or product-strategy heritage: discovery, opportunity sizing, roadmap shaping, prototyping, and stakeholder alignment — ideally on products whose core behaviour is AI rather than conventional software.
Preferred skills:
• Hands on with the AI platform ecosystem as a daily practitioner: fluent in how the landscape is categorised, where the category boundaries actually fall, and which capabilities are genuinely distinct from each other.
• Able to evaluate from first principles and to design the evaluation itself: set the hypothesis, the success bar, the comparison set, and the decision date, and defend the method to engineers and vendors alike.
• A proven record of retiring and consolidating technology, including at least one tool killed on evidence.
#AGTech
Skills
AI Platforms, Artificial Intelligence, Change Management, Data Analysis, Feature Prioritization, Machine Learning (ML), Machine Learning Model Management, ML Platforms, Model Evaluation, Performance Analysis, Product Delivery, Product Design, Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), Product Roadmapping, Product Strategies, Roadmap Development, Statistical Analysis, User Needs Analysis
Why GSK?
Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.
GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.
People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people.

• Write crisp product specs that identify the problem, set goals, and define success metrics so design and engineering can build with clarity.
• Encode the craft of expert SEO and GEO operators into product: AI workflows, agents, and automations that make good work repeatable.
• Work hand in hand with services teams to translate real operational workflows into scalable product, and drive the change management that adoption requires.
• Deconstruct complex problems with technical depth and a steady diet of product usage data to inform the roadmap.
• Practice build versus buy, and partner with third parties where integrations add scalable functionality faster.
What you bring to the table
We care more about what you have built and owned than about a strict year count.
• You have been a founder. You have founded or co-founded a software company and played a hybrid role across its technical and business sides.
• You have done 0 to 1 and 1 to 10. You have launched enterprise products, SaaS or services, and scaled the ones that worked.
• You know B2B and the US market. You have built B2B products and worked closely with US customers, and you understand how enterprise buyers and marketing teams there evaluate, adopt, and expect to be supported.
• You think beyond pure SaaS. You understand Service as a Software thinking and are comfortable building product around services, workflows, and the change management that transformation requires.
• You move fast and think sharply. You ship quickly, iterate in tight loops, and stay scrappy when the situation calls for it.
• You are technical enough. You have strong familiarity with APIs, authentication, and integrations, and have built enterprise products that required third-party integrations.
• You deconstruct complexity. You break down hard problems, spot patterns, and take a data-driven approach to solutions.
• You write and persuade well. You write clearly about product concepts and plans, and you lead through clarity and conviction, not authority.
• You work shoulder to shoulder. You are at home with data science, engineering, design, and customer success, and you build real relationships with customers and stakeholders.
Why this role matters
Most product roles add features to a finished category. This one helps define a new one. Atlas is the bet that organic growth becomes an agentic system: deep enough in craft that a general model cannot match it, and intelligent enough that a super agent can operate it.
If you have built a company before, want to build again without starting from zero on everything, and want to ship fast against a genuinely large idea, this is the seat.

The Senior Product Manager, Agentic Application owns the product strategy, roadmap, and execution for an agentic AI application that automates insurance product configuration for Duck Creek carriers. description:
Who are we?
Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.
A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.
A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.
Job Summary
This is a senior individual contributor role with broad influence across the company. You will own the product strategy for Equinix's conversational AI and assistant platforms — chat, voice, and agentic interfaces that employees, customers, and partners interact with directly. You will work closely with engineering and architecture teams on technical decisions while also helping executives understand business implications, investment choices, and risk.
You will serve as a conversational AI product leader across Go to Market, Operations, Product, and Corporate functions. Depending on the initiative, you may advise business leaders, partner with product and engineering teams, or directly lead product strategy and delivery for conversational experiences and the platform capabilities that power them.
The conversational AI market is changing quickly — from single-turn chatbots to multi-agent, tool-using assistants. An important part of this role is evaluating new conversational AI technologies, identifying which capabilities are relevant to Equinix, and translating them into practical product and platform investment decisions.
Responsibilities
Conversational AI, Cloud, and Data Architecture
• Bring strong working knowledge of conversational AI, dialogue systems, agent orchestration, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise data architecture to product and platform decisions
• Partner with engineering and architecture teams to evaluate large language model architectures, conversational agent design patterns (orchestrator/worker, multi-agent handoff, tool calling), cloud deployment approaches, and enterprise data pipelines
• Participate meaningfully in technical and architecture reviews, as well as product and roadmap discussions for the conversational platform
• Translate technical choices, constraints, and risks into clear business implications that leaders can understand and act on
• Help ensure conversational AI products are designed for enterprise scale, security, reliability, multi-channel support (chat, voice, embedded assistants), and reuse across business functions
Conversation Design, Model Strategy, and Deployment

Platform Reliability and Responsible AI

• Establish requirements that support traceability, explainability, auditability, fairness, privacy, and regulatory compliance across conversational interactions

• Partner with Design to create clear conversational UX that explains how AI is being used, manages user expectations, and provides appropriate review, control, hand-off to a human, and approval within the conversation itself
Product Decisions and Risk Management

• Help teams identify risks early — including hallucination, unintended actions, and improper data exposure in conversational contexts — and determine the appropriate level of governance and human oversight

Executive and Cross Functional Leadership
• Build alignment across Product, Engineering, Architecture, Legal, Information Security, Data, Design, and business functions on the conversational AI roadmap

title: Senior Product Manager
description:
Organization OverviewCompany Description
QAD is a leading provider of ERP solutions purpose-built for manufacturing industries — automotive, life sciences, food & beverage, high tech, and industrial. Serving thousands of global manufacturers, QAD's Adaptive Manufacturing Cloud helps companies operate with greater precision, agility, and intelligence.
QAD's AI Platform is the domain intelligence layer that sits between the ERP and autonomous AI agents. It encodes what manufacturing data means, governs what agents are permitted to do, and makes every autonomous decision traceable and accountable — transforming QAD from a system of record into a system of action.
Job Description
This role owns the full product lifecycle for QAD's Copilot, Search, and Conversational Analytics capabilities — from architecture through to market launch. You will define what gets built, why it matters to manufacturing users, and how it reaches them: shaping the product vision, driving engineering delivery, and partnering with GTM to ensure adoption.
The intelligence that powers these surfaces — how queries are understood, how manufacturing context is assembled, how data is retrieved, and how responses are generated — is where QAD's AI moat is built. You will need to engage deeply with these layers, not as an engineer but as the product owner who defines the contracts, quality standards, and sequencing decisions that determine whether they work in production at enterprise scale.
You will report to the Head of Platform Product, with day-to-day direction from the Director of the AI Platform org. This role is evaluated through the quality of your product thinking, your influence on engineering direction, and the outcomes you drive in the market.
The Opportunity
Manufacturing users today cannot query their own operations without analysts, BI tools, or pre-built reports. QAD's AI platform changes this — but only if the Copilot and Search layer is built correctly and lands with users. You will own both sides of that equation.
• Define the semantic search and conversational analytics product that allows manufacturing users to query operational data — orders, inventory, suppliers, quality records — in natural language, without SQL or BI expertise
• Own the intelligence contract: how queries are understood, how manufacturing context is assembled, how retrieval is orchestrated, and how responses are grounded in governed data — the foundational decisions that determine product quality at scale
• Drive the Copilot from concept to customer — including the contextual layer architecture, the grounding contract against the platform's Semantic Layer, and the GTM motion that gets it adopted in manufacturing workflows
• Build the feedback loops that make the product smarter over time: how recurring query patterns surface ontology gaps, how session analytics drive prioritisation, and how discovery findings translate into product improvements
• Establish QAD's conversational analytics presence in market — working with GTM to define positioning, enablement, and the narrative that differentiates QAD's intelligence layer from horizontal AI tools
Key Responsibilities
Copilot & Conversational Analytics
• Own the product definition for QAD's Copilot: how queries are understood, context assembled, data retrieved, and responses generated — specifying the contracts that engineering builds against
• Define the grounding contract: the rules that ensure every Copilot response cites governed manufacturing data, not hallucinated inference — including confidence signalling and graceful fallback behaviour
• Drive the conversational analytics strategy: how natural language queries translate into analytical results across manufacturing data domains without exposing SQL or BI complexity to the user
• Specify the disambiguation model: how the Copilot handles ambiguous queries, missing context, and conflicting data signals in real manufacturing workflows
Search
• Own the product definition for QAD's semantic search layer: indexing strategy, query understanding, entity recognition, ranking, and result structure across manufacturing data domains
• Define the search intent taxonomy — operational (find order, trace shipment), analytical (show trends, compare periods), and diagnostic (why is this delayed, what caused this variance) — and specify result formats by intent type
• Drive the federated search architecture: how results from ERP operational data, analytical stores, and the knowledge graph are ranked and merged into a coherent, useful response
Discovery, Delivery & GTM
• Maintain a structured customer discovery programme — extracting real manufacturing query patterns and translating findings into specific product and architecture implications
• Own the product backlog: writing stories to Staff Engineer level of specificity — API contracts, state machines, data flows, edge cases — that engineering can build without verbal clarification
• Partner with GTM to define the launch and adoption strategy for Copilot and Search: positioning, sales enablement, onboarding playbooks, and the narrative that lands with manufacturing buyers
• Define the quality framework for these surfaces: what signals matter for product performance — retrieval relevance, grounding rate, latency distribution — and how they inform roadmap decisions
Stakeholder Management & Managing Up
• Proactively surface dependencies, risks, and scope changes to the Director and Head of Platform Product — with a resolution proposal, not just an escalation
• Communicate product and architecture decisions clearly to non-technical stakeholders — translating trade-offs into business implications without jargon
• Build credibility with Engineering, Architecture, and GTM through the quality and precision of written work
Qualifications
Product Experience
• 7–12 years in product management, with significant time owning AI-powered, search, or analytics products in enterprise B2B environments — from definition through production launch
• Proven track record owning the full product lifecycle: customer discovery, specification, engineering delivery, and GTM — not just one slice
• Experience working in matrixed organisations — driving outcomes across Platform, Engineering, Architecture, and GTM without direct authority
• Evidence of structured discovery practice applied to a technical product surface — ability to extract product implications from user research, not just UX insights
Core Technical Depth — Required
These are the primary technical domains this role owns. Strong command is expected from day one.
• Semantic search architecture: indexing strategy, query understanding, entity recognition, ranking models, and relevance evaluation at enterprise scale
• Conversational AI product design: how natural language queries are translated into structured analytical results across complex, domain-specific data without exposing backend complexity to users
• LLM-integrated product specification: grounding strategies, hallucination mitigation, response quality gates, and context window management — sufficient to define product contracts engineering builds against
• Data platform fluency: OLAP vs operational DB reads, federated search across heterogeneous stores, and how data freshness constraints affect product quality — sufficient to hold authoritative conversations with data engineers
• SQL and data modelling: sufficient to validate query plans, understand schema implications, and reason through retrieval architecture trade-offs
Working Familiarity — Expected to Grow Into
These domains sit in adjacent platform layers that Copilot and Search consume. Deep expertise is not required on day one, but working fluency is expected — and will expand as the platform scales toward agentic capabilities.
• Intent detection and query understanding pipelines: how user inputs are parsed, classified, and routed across platform layers
• Context assembly and packaging: how metric definitions, entity relationships, and business rules are structured and passed downstream at inference time
• Session and state management: conversation continuity, context windowing across multi-turn interactions, and memory summarisation patterns
• Human-in-the-loop design: approval workflows, confidence thresholds, and escalation paths where AI-generated outputs require human validation before action
Competency Expectations
This role is calibrated to a Staff PM equivalent. Across QAD's four PM competency pillars:
• Product Execution — Expert: Feature specification to Staff Engineer fidelity, end-to-end delivery ownership, and AI-specific quality gates (grounding rate, retrieval relevance, latency SLAs)
• Customer Insight — Expert: Translates discovery and usage data into product decisions. Understands that conversational UX quality is determined by the intelligence layer beneath it
• Product Strategy — Expert on vision and roadmapping; Intermediate on strategic impact, with a clear growth path toward Advanced as the platform scales
• Influencing People — Intermediate on stakeholder management and managing up, growing toward Advanced. No people management expectation; growth path is toward leading a TPO as the surface scales
Behavioural Signals — Critical
• Writes first, asks second — produces a concrete proposal or spec draft before escalating ambiguity
• Distinguishes clearly between what is known, assumed, and needs validation — and acts accordingly
• Comfortable operating without a playbook — defines the approach in novel problem spaces
• Gravitates toward precision in language and specification — understands that ambiguous requirements are a form of technical debt
Manufacturing Or ERP Context — Preferred
• Familiarity with manufacturing ERP data models (inventory, orders, procurement, quality) is a strong plus; not required if technical depth and learning velocity are demonstrated
• Experience with operational analytics or supply chain intelligence products is valued, especially where the product involved translating domain-specific data into natural language interfaces
Additional Information
• End-to-end ownership: You define what gets built and ensure it lands — from intelligence layer architecture to GTM motion and customer adoption
• High-leverage surface: Copilot and Search are the primary interface through which manufacturing users experience QAD's AI platform. The decisions you make here compound across the platform
• Technical depth valued: Specification quality is the primary currency of influence in this environment. Strong product thinking is recognised and rewarded
• Growth trajectory: Clear path from Staff PM to broader intelligence surface ownership — including deeper agentic platform exposure — and over time, a small team
• Pune platform hub: QAD is actively expanding its platform engineering and product capabilities in India — you will be a founding voice in that growth
About QAD
QAD | Redzone is redefining manufacturing and supply chains through its intelligent, adaptive platform that connects people, processes, and data into a single System of Action. With three core pillars — Redzone (frontline empowerment), Adaptive Applications (the intelligent backbone), and Champion AI (Agentic AI for manufacturing) — QAD | Redzone helps manufacturers operate with Champion Pace, achieving measurable productivity, resilience, and growth in just 90 days.
QAD is committed to ensuring that every employee feels they work in an environment that values their contributions, respects their unique perspectives and provides opportunities for growth regardless of background. QAD’s DEI program is driving higher levels of diversity, equity and inclusion so that employees can bring their whole self to work.
We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class.

title: Product Manager
description:
Product Manager – AI-Native Strategy Execution
Location - Bangalore
About GravityONE
GravityONE is an AI-native technology company building the next generation of products for strategy, decision-making and execution. We work at the intersection of AI, strategy, data and enterprise workflows, helping organisations move beyond traditional dashboards and disconnected tools towards intelligent systems that can help leaders and teams plan, decide, coordinate and act.
Our products are designed for complex environments where strategy needs to translate into measurable outcomes—with the right context, governance, intelligence and accountability built into the way organisations operate.
One of our core products, StrategyDotZero, is building an AI-native strategy-execution platform for governments and enterprises. We help executives, Strategy Offices, PMOs and transformation teams connect strategy, planning, performance, portfolios and delivery into one intelligence-enabled operating environment.
Our ambition is to move beyond dashboards and workflow tools—to create governed digital experts and agentic workflows that help organisations plan, decide, coordinate and act with greater confidence.
The Role
We are seeking an exceptional, hands-on Product Manager to turn this vision into a focused, market-ready product.
You will sit at the intersection of strategy, design, data, analytics and AI: shaping product direction, rapidly testing concepts with customers, and working closely with engineering, AI and growth teams to turn complex problems into elegant, adoptable capabilities.
This is a build-stage role for someone who enjoys ambiguity, moves quickly and can balance bold product thinking with disciplined execution. We are particularly interested in candidates who bring the structured problem-solving and transformation mindset of top-tier consulting, combined with strong product judgement and the ability to build and ship.
What you will do
• Translate the StrategyDotZero vision into clear product strategy, customer journeys, MVPs, roadmaps and fortnightly release plans.
• Shape AI-native experiences across strategy, planning, portfolio management, PMO, performance, benefits, risk and executive decision support.
• Define how agentic workflows, LLM-enabled generation, analytics, enterprise data and human approval work together in practical product experiences.
• Rapidly create wireframes, clickable prototypes, concept demonstrations and lightweight proof-of-value solutions to test ideas with users before building at scale.
• Lead product discovery with executives, PMO leaders, strategy teams and delivery practitioners; identify high-value problems, validate assumptions and translate insight into product decisions.
• Write high-quality user stories, functional specifications, acceptance criteria, workflow logic and release documentation that engineering teams can build with confidence.
• Work closely with engineers and AI specialists to define fit-for-purpose agent behaviours, inputs, outputs, controls, evaluation criteria and user feedback loops.
• Ensure every capability is enterprise-ready: role-based access, source evidence, data quality, confidence indicators, auditability and human approval for material decisions or changes.
• Prioritise the roadmap using customer value, strategic differentiation, delivery effort, technical dependencies and commercial potential.
• Run agile planning, backlog refinement, sprint reviews, release readiness and post-release learning with discipline and pace.
• Partner with growth and customer teams to shape demos, value narratives, pilots, customer feedback loops and product-market fit.
What we are looking for
• 5+ years of experience in product management, product design, strategy/technology consulting or a related product-building role.
• MBA from a reputed institution, preferably with a focus on strategy, technology, operations or a related discipline.
• Prior experience with a Big 4 consulting firm (Deloitte, PwC, EY or KPMG) or a strong strategy/management consulting environment is highly preferred. We value candidates who have developed strong structured problem-solving, executive communication, business transformation and stakeholder management skills and can apply that thinking to product development.
• Experience building B2B, enterprise SaaS, workflow, analytics, data or AI-enabled products—ideally in complex, regulated or multi-stakeholder environments.
• Strong understanding of strategy execution, planning, PMO, portfolio management, transformation, performance or operational governance; deep expertise in every domain is not required, but curiosity and rapid learning are.
• Practical familiarity with AI product patterns: LLMs, RAG, structured outputs, agentic workflows, enterprise data context, human-in-the-loop design, evaluation and feedback loops.
• Strong UX and design judgement, with the ability to use tools such as Figma and AI-assisted prototyping tools to make concepts tangible quickly.
• Comfortable working with data, dashboards, integrations, APIs and enterprise workflow concepts; able to speak credibly with engineers without needing to be a full-time developer.
• Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to move comfortably between a client executive, product designer, engineer and delivery practitioner.
• A strong bias toward action: able to frame a problem, form a hypothesis, prototype, test, learn and improve within days—not months.
• Comfortable in a lean, high-growth environment where ownership is broad, priorities evolve and quality still matters.
What success looks like
• A focused, differentiated product roadmap that converts the StrategyDotZero vision into commercially valuable releases.
• Fast, evidence-led product discovery with customers and a regular cadence of validated prototypes and shipped capabilities.
• Clear and reusable product patterns for enterprise AI: governed agents, source-grounded outputs, human approvals and actionable workflows.
• Strong alignment between product, engineering, AI, growth and client teams.
• A platform that customers experience not as another PMO tool, but as an intelligence layer that improves the quality and speed of strategy execution.
• A product leader who brings together consulting rigour, product thinking, AI fluency and execution discipline to turn complex enterprise problems into simple, valuable products.
If you think this
If you think this role is for you, we’d love to hear from you.
Send your profile to: ashwini.vagadia@gravityone.ai

title: Principal Product Manager
description:

Our team builds and owns the quality of some of the most widely used AI and search experiences in Microsoft 365 — Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and enterprise search across Outlook, Teams, OneDrive/SharePoint and Copilot Search — serving billions of queries every month. title: LEAD PRODUCT AI & DIGITAL PLATFORM-INDIA
description:
The Role
We're seeking a Product Owner , AI, Agentic Capabilities & Customer Experience to define and execute the strategy for bringing advanced and proactive AI capabilities, including Agentic AI, to the Lumen Customer Portal and enterprise digital experiences. This critical role is about building the next generation of digital service, moving the customer experience from interaction-first to resolution-first, by leveraging AI and autonomous (agentic) capabilities to solve complex B2B customer issues end-to-end and drive significant operational efficiency. This individual will own the Generative AI and Agentic Roadmap and its required foundational platform components, ensuring seamless integration into the enterprise customer portal, developer portal, and underlying API products. The individual in this role collaborates closely with cross-functional teams to drive development and integration, establish and maintain alignment between the customer experience and development roadmaps, and serve as a champion for safe, reliable, and high-quality autonomous experiences.
The Main Responsibilities
• Architecting the AI Future: Work collaboratively and cross-functionally to define the vision for the Lumen Platform's Generative AI strategy, specifically focusing on how Large Language Models (LLMs) and autonomous/agentic systems can resolve complex B2B customer issues end-to-end, aligned with organizational goals and strategic priorities.
• Bridging Technical & Business Needs: Translate complex B2B customer journeys and business requirements (e.g., ticket creation, service modification, billing inquiries) into clear, actionable technical specifications for AI Agents, conversational interfaces, and workflow automation systems and their required underlying Tooling/APIs and orchestration logic.
• Deep Customer & AI Feedback Engagement: Engage regularly with customers and platform users to capture real-world feedback on AI accuracy, trust, and usability. Leverage these insights to inform the Agentic AI continuous learning and refinement roadmap, ensuring high user satisfaction (CSAT/NPS).
• Championing the AI Tooling Layer: Advocate for and drive an API-first strategy to ensure the platform provides a robust, governed, and structured Tooling Layer that AI models and autonomous agents can reliably call for action (e.g., defining API standards, taxonomy, and latency requirements for AI consumption).
• Driving AI Execution & Governance: Lead execution of the Generative AI and Agentic roadmap, defining detailed capabilities, LLM integration requirements, and Guardrails & Safety protocols (including Prompt Injection Prevention, data masking, and compliance checks) to mitigate risks like hallucination and data leakage.
• AI Performance & Lifecycle Management: Implement rigorous AI Governance and MLOps practices. Define and track key performance indicators including Task Success Rate, Hallucination Rate, Cost Per Interaction (CPI), and Agent Latency, ensuring solutions are robust, and changes are vetted against these metrics before release. Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities to improve the end-to-end roadmap execution process, driving key learnings back into the organization.
What We Look For In a Candidate
• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent education and experience in a relevant technical discipline (e.g., Computer Science, Engineering); master's degree is a plus.
• 8+ years of progressive experience in Technical Product Management or Software Engineering, including 3+ years directly defining and launching Generative AI capabilities (specifically Agentic AI, large-scale conversational interfaces, or autonomous workflows).
• Deep expertise in Generative AI architectures, Large Language Models (LLMs), RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) patterns, and the design of AI 'tools' or functions for autonomous agents.
• Deep technical knowledge and understanding of API design principles (REST, GraphQL, Event Driven APIs), microservices architecture, and cloud platforms.
• Extensive experience with digital platforms, enterprise customer portals, and/or complex web applications, coupled with strong working knowledge of user experience design & research, and modern software development methodologies (Agile, DevOps).
• Proven ability to analyze complex technical data, identify and troubleshoot intricate technical issues, and develop scalable solutions that directly impact the customer and developer experience on the platform.
• Outstanding communication and interpersonal skills that enable effective collaboration with diverse technical and non-technical teams, stakeholders, and customers. Ability to create clarity and drive focus in complex and dynamic technical contexts up, down, and across the organization.
• Ability to manage and lead multiple technical priorities and projects while delivering against tight timelines in a complex and dynamic environment.

title: Product Marketing Manager
description:
Enterprise Bot is the leading provider of GenAI, Conversational AI and automation software, headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland.
Our intelligent virtual assistants and automation tools help companies increase efficiency, reduce costs, and deliver exceptional customer experiences in industries such as banking, insurance, and logistics. Our mission is to become the world's leading provider of AI-powered automation software within the next five years.
We work with leading companies such as SIX Group (Swiss Stock Exchange), SWICA, Generali and others to improve customer interactions and automate business processes using our state-of-the-art Conversational AI technology.
Our global team comprises more than 70 highly qualified professionals from diverse backgrounds.
We foster an open, progressive company culture with state-of-the-art technology and flat hierarchies. At Enterprise Bot, you'll experience a unique blend of passion, ambition, challenge, and fun.
Tasks
Enterprise Bot builds agentic AI for voice, chat, email and messaging, deployed by regulated enterprises across Europe, including financial services, insurance and public-sector organisations. We are Swiss-headquartered, which shapes how we approach data sovereignty, privacy and compliance.
The AI market is saturated. New tools launch constantly, and enterprise buyers are struggling to tell platforms apart from wrappers. This role exists to make sure Enterprise Bot is never evaluated as just another AI product. You will own our competitive intelligence, sharpen our positioning, take our product and platform releases to market, advise Product on what the market is telling us, and make all of it consistent in every country we sell in.
This is a builder's role. There is no existing product marketing function, so you will create it.
What you'll own
Product and platform launches, end to end
• Own the full launch lifecycle for products, platform releases and major features, from early planning through to post-launch performance review
• Define launch tiering, so that a platform-level release and a minor feature receive proportionate investment and internal attention
• Build the launch narrative and the supporting asset set: positioning brief, messaging framework, demo narrative, website and campaign copy, release notes, customer communications and partner briefing material
• Run cross-functional launch readiness across Product, Engineering, Sales, Pre-Sales, Customer Success, Partnerships and Support, including a clear go or no-go checkpoint
• Coordinate with Demand Generation on launch campaigns, and with Partnerships on integrator, BPO and technology partner enablement
• Define launch success metrics up front, including adoption, pipeline influenced, sales confidence and competitive win rate, then report against them and feed the findings into the next launch
• Own the internal launch calendar and keep it aligned with the product release cadence, so that go-to-market readiness is never the constraint on shipping
Roadmap collaboration (advisory)
Product owns roadmap prioritisation. Your role is to make sure those decisions are made with clear commercial and competitive evidence in front of them.
• Bring structured market, competitive and buyer evidence into roadmap discussions, so that prioritisation is informed by what the market is telling us rather than by opinion
• Maintain a live view of competitive feature gaps and buyer requirements, particularly around omnichannel orchestration, deployment flexibility, multilingual coverage and compliance, and share it with Product on a regular cadence
• Feed win/loss findings and recurring RFP requirement patterns into the roadmap process as input
• Review planned roadmap items from a market-facing perspective and flag early where a capability will be difficult to differentiate or to sell
• Support roadmap communication to customers, prospects and partners, balancing transparency against commitment risk
Competitive intelligence
• Build and maintain a structured view of the competitive landscape across manufacturers, integrators and BPOs, including which players are competitors, which are partner candidates, and which are both
• Establish a formal Win/Loss Analysis programme: define the loss-cause taxonomy, run the debriefs, and turn the findings into action rather than anecdote
• Mine RFP responses as the primary source of competitive truth, since that is where head-to-head comparison actually happens
• Produce and maintain battlecards, objection-handling guides and competitive teardowns that sales can use without translation
Positioning and messaging
• Own the core positioning and unify it across geographies. Messaging varies by country today, and that inconsistency costs us
• Translate technical differentiators into buyer-facing value: omnichannel orchestration on a single knowledge and action layer, model-agnostic architecture, on-premise and sovereign deployment options, native multilingual handling, and European compliance readiness
• Adapt positioning to local market realities (Spain, Switzerland, DACH and wider Europe) without fragmenting the core narrative
• Define and maintain the messaging hierarchy, proof points and reference stories
Website narrative and messaging
You own what the website says. Demand Generation owns the platform it says it on, and Content owns localisation into market languages.
• Own the messaging and narrative on product, solution and platform pages, so that the site reflects current positioning rather than the positioning of the last launch
• Propose the information architecture and the overall site narrative, including how the platform story is told across pages, and work with Demand Generation to implement it
• Review core pages against positioning on a defined cadence, and keep them current between launches rather than only at launch
• Brief Content on source messaging and market nuance for localisation, and review localised pages for positioning accuracy
• Work with Demand Generation where page messaging and conversion goals pull in different directions, and resolve it on evidence
Sales enablement
• Build enablement assets, including pitch decks, one-pagers, demo narratives, and ROI and cost-comparison material
• Support pricing and packaging decisions with competitive and buyer input, including how implementation and professional services are presented in commercial proposals
• Support analyst relations, RFP content libraries and industry event messaging
• Run enablement sessions so that new positioning and new releases actually reach the field, and check that they land
Voice of the market
• Run structured customer and prospect interviews to keep positioning grounded in what buyers actually say
• Feed market and competitive signal back into product prioritisation on a regular cadence
Requirements
Required
• 5+ years in product marketing within B2B technology, SaaS or enterprise software
• Demonstrable experience marketing to enterprise buyers with long, multi-stakeholder sales cycles
• Proven ownership of product and platform launches end to end, not only the asset production within someone else’s launch plan
• Direct working experience with Product and Engineering teams, including contributing market and competitive evidence to roadmap discussions
• Proven ownership of competitive analysis and positioning, not only campaign execution
• Experience owning product and solution page messaging on a company website, including keeping it aligned to positioning over time
• Strong written English, with the ability to turn technical capability into commercial argument
• Experience working with distributed sales teams across multiple countries
• Comfort operating with European working hours for part of the day
Strongly preferred
• Background in conversational AI, CCaaS, contact centre technology, automation or adjacent categories
• Experience marketing into regulated industries such as financial services, insurance, healthcare or public sector
• Familiarity with European compliance frameworks (GDPR, DORA and sector certifications) as buying criteria
• Experience with on-premise or hybrid deployment models, not SaaS only
• Experience launching platform products rather than single-channel point solutions
• Exposure to partner and channel go-to-market
How we'll know you're the right fit
• You can look at a crowded category and articulate why one product is structurally different, not simply better marketed
• You can walk us through a launch you owned end to end, including what you would do differently
• You have run a win/loss programme, or built one from nothing
• You can influence a roadmap you do not control by bringing evidence rather than pressure, and you are equally comfortable telling Sales when the positioning is wrong.
First 90 days
• Days 1 to 30: Competitive landscape mapped and classified. Ten win/loss interviews completed across recent deals. Launch process and release cadence understood, with current gaps documented.
• Days 31 to 60: Core positioning documented and validated with the CEO and regional sales leads. First battlecards in the hands of sales. Launch framework and tiering agreed with Product.
• Days 61 to 90: Unified messaging framework rolled out across markets. Win/loss programme running on a repeatable cadence. First launch owned end to end under the new framework, with success metrics reported.
Benefits
• Shape a function from the ground up – Build Enterprise Bot's first Product Marketing function and have a direct impact on product strategy, positioning and go-to-market.
• Work with cutting-edge AI – Help define the market narrative for an enterprise-grade agentic AI platform used by leading financial services, insurance and public sector organisations across Europe.
• Global exposure – Collaborate daily with Product, Engineering and commercial teams across Switzerland, Spain, Poland, the UK and other European markets.
• High ownership, low bureaucracy – Take ownership of launches, competitive strategy and messaging, with the autonomy to influence business decisions and work directly with senior leadership.
• Competitive salary and performance-based incentives – We offer a competitive compensation package aligned to experience and impact.
This is a unique opportunity to build a Product Marketing function from the ground up and influence how Enterprise Bot competes and grows across Europe. If that excites you, we'd love to hear from you.
