Job Description
Role summary
The Senior Staff Software Engineer (IC5) on HR Service Delivery sets and owns the technical direction for model-driven capability across the HR domain and the surfaces adjacent domains build on top of it. The work is agentic and conversational experiences that interpret an employee's, manager's, or HR agent's intent, reason over profile, case, catalog, policy, and knowledge context, invoke tools, and act on the user's behalf — but the unit of ownership is the architecture, the standards, and the evaluation infrastructure that let multiple teams ship those experiences safely, not a set of features.
This is not a machine learning or AI research role; the engineer does not train foundation models. It is also distinct from traditional staff-level full-stack engineering, where systems follow deterministic logic rather than selecting execution paths at runtime. Two consequences shape the work. First, the most important logic often lives in natural language — instructions, prompts, tool descriptions, guardrails, escalation rules — which must be engineered, versioned, and reviewed with the same discipline as code, and which needs an architecture once more than one team is authoring it. Second, because behavior is probabilistic, correctness is established by measuring behavior at scale rather than by asserting fixed outputs, which makes evaluation a platform investment rather than a per-feature activity.
HR sharpens both points along two independent axes.
Accuracy. An agent answering on payroll, benefits, leave, or a lifecycle event touches statutory entitlement, jurisdiction-specific policy, and an employee's pay. A confidently wrong output is not a bad answer; it is a missed enrollment window or an incorrect leave balance acted on in good faith.
Audience. HR data is among the most sensitive on the platform, and correctness of content is not sufficient. An answer grounded in a record or knowledge article the requestor is not entitled to read is a data exposure even when every fact in it is true, and manager-scope and employee-scope views of the same question have different correct answers. Enforcement belongs in the retrieval and tool layer, not in a request to the model, and at this level you own that being true by construction across every team building in the domain.
The distinguishing expectation at IC5 is that the hardest problems arrive unframed. You decide what the domain should do about them, commit the organization to an approach, and are accountable for that approach across releases — including for the decisions that turn out wrong.
What you do Set the AI architecture for the domain
Own the architecture of model-driven capability across the employee lifecycle: how agents are decomposed and composed, where reasoning happens, how context is assembled and bounded, how tools are exposed and described, and how autonomy is delegated and revoked. Establish the reference patterns other teams build against, and the boundaries between what is a shared platform concern and what each product area owns. Make the calls with multi-release consequences — model selection and migration, orchestration approach, build-versus-adopt, and the cost, latency, and quality tradeoffs behind each — and own the outcome.
Define where autonomy goes, and where it does not
Decide, as a matter of domain policy rather than per-feature design, which HR actions an agent may take, which require a human decision point, and which no agent should attempt. Anything that changes pay, employment status, or a restricted record, and anything touching employee relations or investigation, needs a human in the path by construction. Then build the mechanisms that make those constraints structural and hard to violate accidentally, so that a team shipping a new capability inherits the boundary instead of re-deriving it. You hold the authority to refuse a shipping decision on these grounds, and are expected to use it.
Own the shared instruction and tool-description architecture
HRSD ships as product: customers configure, extend, and override the instruction and tool surface on their own instances, and adjacent domains build against it. Treat it as a versioned contract with upgrade-safe extension points, deprecation paths, and compatibility guarantees. Own how that surface is structured, reviewed, and evolved across teams — including the authoring standards, the review bar, and the regression coverage that make natural-language logic maintainable at organizational scale rather than only within one codebase.
Build the evaluation infrastructure the organization ships against
Own evaluation as leverage: the golden datasets, multi-turn suites, judge calibration, CI gates, and drift detection that let many teams change behavior safely and quickly. Extend coverage to the HR-specific failure classes — access-boundary violations in retrieval and citation, cross-scope leakage, jurisdictional and policy-variant correctness — and keep it meaningful across the range of customer configurations rather than a single reference environment. Define the resolution, containment, and quality metrics the domain is measured on, be the person who can say whether they are instrumented correctly, and raise the standard of evidence required before a behavioral change ships.
Frame problems the organization has not yet framed
Identify the risks, gaps, and structural weaknesses in model-driven behavior that no one has articulated yet, quantify them, and drive them to a decision. This includes the failure classes that only appear at scale or in specific customer environments, the second-order consequences of a model or platform change, and the places where current practice will not survive the next generation of capability. Bring these to product and engineering leadership with the analysis and the recommendation, not the problem alone.
Direct AI coding agents, and set how the organization does
Convert ambiguous problem statements into testable specifications with explicit scope, constraints, non-goals, and acceptance criteria; decompose work into agent-sized tasks; and supervise parallel workstreams. Beyond your own delivery, define what accountable agent-assisted engineering looks like for the domain — specification standards, review expectations, verification harnesses — and hold the line on it. You own the result regardless of what produced it, and you own the norm.
Own production quality, safety, and reliability across the domain
Own the observability and safety posture for agentic behavior: conversation quality, containment, hallucination rate, tool-selection error, unsafe or unauthorized action, and the paths where user-supplied content — case notes, inbound email, attachments, authored knowledge — enters agent context as an injection vector. Because HR conversation content is itself restricted, design diagnosis that works without exposing what was said. Lead root-cause analysis on the incidents no one else can resolve, hold the distinction between a genuine model failure and a platform or configuration failure presenting as one, and close the loop from production failure back into specification and evaluation.
Deliver hands-on where it matters
Stay in the code on the load-bearing parts: the hard integration, the risky migration, the prototype that settles an architectural argument, the incident nobody else can unblock. Delivery at this level is selective and deliberate rather than continuous, and the expectation is that your hands-on work resolves uncertainty for others rather than absorbing feature scope.
Influence beyond the team
Represent the domain's technical position to engineering and product leadership, to customers, and to partner organizations. Communicate capability and risk to non-engineering audiences without flattening either. Build alignment across teams that do not report to you and whose priorities compete. Grow staff-level engineers, raise the bar in technical review and hiring, and make the domain's practices around instruction authoring, evaluation, and accountable agent use durable enough to outlast your involvement in any one project.
Qualifications
Required experience and skills
• Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.
• 12+ years software engineering experience (backend, frontend, or full stack) 
• Strong JavaScript/Node.js, React and API integration skills 
• Automated testing (unit + integration) and CI/CD pipeline experience 
• Solid understanding of data modelling and query optimization 
• Agentic delivery experience: 
• Hands-on experience with AI/GenAI or ML-driven features (LLM prompting, NLU, classification models, or similar) 
• Hands-on experience with LLM-integrated features: prompt design, context injection, output tuning, guardrails. 
• Experience with NLU/intent classification or conversational AI systems 
• Familiarity with ML-driven automation (classification, clustering, recommendation systems) 
• Production AI integration. Experience integrating large language model APIs and retrieval-grounded features, including agent orchestration, tool and function calling, and structured output enforcement. 
• Applied machine learning literacy. A working command of the concepts that govern how these systems behave — evaluation, embeddings, and the probabilistic output and failure modes of modern models — sufficient to reason about, debug, and verify model-driven behaviour in production. 
• Accountable use of AI coding agents. Current, effective use of AI coding assistants and agents with evidence of accountable delivery: precise specification, critical review of generated output, and verification harnesses. 
• Operational experience. Hands-on CI/CD, containerized workloads, and observability experience, plus direct on-call and incident-command experience with customer-facing systems. 
• Mentorship. Demonstrated mentorship of less-experienced engineers and a record of raising quality through code review. 
• Education. Bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degrees are a plus but not a substitute for a record of shipping reliable AI-native applications.
Preferred Experience
• HR domain depth. HR case management, the employee lifecycle, or payroll, benefits, leave, and absence, at a depth sufficient to challenge a requirement rather than only implement it — including why the same policy question resolves differently by jurisdiction, employment type, or plan year. 
• HCM and downstream integration. Integration with core HR, payroll, and benefits systems of record, including the reconciliation and eventual-consistency problems that come with treating an external system as the authority on employment data. 
• Extensible product engineering. Building capability that customers configure, extend, and override on their own instances, where instruction and tool surfaces are versioned contracts rather than internal implementation. 
• Evaluation and observability tooling. Evaluation frameworks, prompt and instruction management tooling, tracing for model-driven applications, and analysis of production transcripts at scale, particularly where transcript content is itself access-restricted. 
• Conversational channel breadth. Employee self-service portals, virtual agent or chat shells, workplace messaging clients, and voice, including handoff between automated and live agents. 
• Conversation design partnership. Working alongside conversation or content designers on dialogue flow, tone, and error-recovery design — with attention to how an HR answer is worded when the subject is the employee's own pay, health coverage, or employment status. 
• Forward deployed delivery. Building against a customer's data, integrations, and channels, and tuning instructions and evaluation sets in their environment. 
• Now Platform depth. Scoped applications, ACLs and platform security rules, Flow Designer, UI Builder, Automated Test Framework, and upgrade-safe extension patterns.

title: Lead Enterprise Solutions Applied AI Engineer
description:
Why UKG
At UKG, the work you do matters. The code you ship, the decisions you make, and the care you show a customer all add up to real impact. Today, tens of millions of workers start and end their days with our workforce operating platform. Helping people get paid, grow in their careers, and shape the future of their industries. That’s what we do.
We never stop learning. We never stop challenging the norm. We push for better, and we celebrate the wins along the way. Here, you’ll get flexibility that’s real, benefits you can count on, and a team that succeeds together. Because at UKG, your work matters—and so do you.
Core Mission
The Lead Applied AI Engineer is a hands-on, forward-deployed technical leader responsible for designing, building, and deploying production-grade agentic AI solutions across the enterprise. The role involves working directly with business units to create autonomous systems that deliver measurable impact. This individual will not only build solutions but also establish standards, reference architectures, and safety guardrails for how agentic AI is developed and scaled responsibly throughout the organization.
The position is for a "builder" who can translate complex business workflows into automated, agent-driven processes while navigating the realities of an enterprise environment, including security, governance, and user trust.
Key Responsibilities
This is a hybrid role-blending hands-on solution delivery with platform-level strategy.
•  Forward-Deployed Solution Delivery (60% of time)
Lead Agentic AI Initiatives: Serve as the embedded technical leader within business units to translate needs into robust, enterprise-integrated agentic AI solutions, overseeing the full lifecycle from idea to implementation and monitoring.
Enterprise System Integration: Connect AI agents to diverse enterprise platforms (e.g., Salesforce, SAP, legacy databases, APIs), ensuring seamless integration and production-ready performance through rapid iteration and troubleshooting.
Pilot Management & Knowledge Transfer: Oversee pilot launches, provide user training, and develop thorough documentation to support smooth adoption and transition of AI solutions to business stakeholders.
•  Agentic System Architecture & Engineering (25% of time)
Design and build multi-agent AI systems that automate complex business processes, emphasizing agent orchestration and human in the loop concepts.
Transform human workflows into agent-first processes, ensuring effective automation while identifying necessary human oversight points.
Develop evaluation tools and optimize solutions for performance and cost, maintaining high quality throughout deployment and operation.
•  Platform Contributions & Standardization (15% of time)
Create Reusable Assets: Extract successful patterns from fieldwork to create libraries, templates, and reference implementations for other teams to use.
Set Enterprise Standards: Define production-ready reference architectures and official checklists for security, reliability, and operability.
Enable Governance & Safety: Partner with Security and Governance teams to embed safety guardrails, audit logging, and compliance checks into core agent architectures.
Mentorship and Enablement: Author best practices, lead technical reviews, and mentor other engineers to help them ship agentic solutions independently.
Required Qualifications
Over 10 years of experience in software engineering. More than 5 years building AI and machine learning systems. 3+ years delivering AI solutions that create real business results in production.
Leadership experience guiding technical direction and aligning teams.
Skilled with large language models (LLMs), prompt engineering, and agent frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex.
Hands-on with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and using tools or functions within AI agents.
Proficient in Python, with strong knowledge of frontend development for agent UIs-React, TypeScript, APIs, authentication, and building reliable production systems.
Experience integrating with business systems (CRMs, ERPs, HR platforms).
Strong understanding of enterprise security, compliance, and data governance.
Deep understanding of OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Azure OpenAI, and agent frameworks such as Microsoft Agent Framework, Vertex AI Agent Builder, and Semantic Kernel.
Knowledge of vector databases like MongoDB, Pinecone, Weaviate, and Qdrant, Graph databased for knowledge representation.
Experienced with cloud services (Azure, GCP), container tools (Docker, Kubernetes), and CI/CD pipelines.
Skilled with logging, tracing, and monitoring tools for AI applications.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Industrial Technology or Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).
Ideal Candidate Profile: Who Thrives in This Role
Builders Over Theorists: You love shipping working software more than debating architecture. You have debugged authentication issues at 2am and resolved production incidents.
Field-Focused Problem Solvers: You get energized by sitting with users, understanding their pain, and building something that makes their day better. You are comfortable with ambiguity and incomplete requirements.
Pragmatic Technologists: You choose boring, reliable solutions over shiny new frameworks. You know when to use an agent and when a simple script is better. You balance innovation with delivery.
Translators: You can explain technical tradeoffs to executives and business requirements to engineers. You bridge worlds.
Standard Setters: You turn one-off successes into repeatable systems—templates, guardrails, evaluation suites, and reference architectures that scale across teams.
Entrepreneurial Mindset: You treat each business unit like a customer. You understand ROI, adoption, and change management matter as much as code quality.
Comfortable with Constraints: You know how to work within enterprise reality—security reviews, compliance requirements, budget constraints—without letting them kill momentum.
Generous Collaborators: You mentor others, share your learnings, and make the team better. You default to clear documentation and proactive communication.
Company Overview
UKG is the Workforce Operating Platform that puts workforce understanding to work. With the world's largest collection of workforce insights, and people-first AI, our ability to reveal unseen ways to build trust, amplify productivity, and empower talent, is unmatched. It's this expertise that equips our customers with the intelligence to solve any challenge in any industry — because great organizations know their workforce is their competitive edge. Learn more at ukg.com.
UKG is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and is committed to promoting diversity and inclusion in the workplace, including the recruitment process.

For individuals with disabilities that need additional assistance at any point in the application and interview process, please email UKGCareers@ukg.com

title: Head - People Success
description:
Head - People Success
Type: Full-time 
Location: Delhi NCR / Bhopal (Remote today; office-based once our India office opens) 
Experience: 15+ YOE in human resources, including proven global team building 
Reports to: President, India 
Manages: People Success function across India and the United States
About Sutra.AI
Sutra.AI is a complete 'Data to Value' AI business transformation platform designed specifically for Business Builders. Unlike other platforms that cater to AI Builders or large enterprises with substantial budgets, Sutra.AI is purpose-built for mid-market businesses without the need of AI expertise. Developed over 4 years, Sutra.AI is a patent-pending fully orchestrated AI SaaS platform. It identifies and executes AI use cases to enhance operational efficiency, customer experience, revenue growth, profitability, innovation, and risk reduction.
Role Overview
The Head - People Success is the single point of accountability for talent acquisition, org design, performance, total rewards, engagement, culture, people operations and statutory compliance across all geographies in which Sutra.AI operates.
The role partners directly with the President (India), the founder and functional heads on structure, hiring sequence and workforce spend. It is expected to challenge those decisions with evidence, not to implement them unquestioned.
Base Location should be Delhi NCR / Bhopal.
What You'll Do
1. Talent Acquisition & Employer Brand
• Build the hiring engine end to end: role scorecards, structured interview loops, calibration standards and interviewer training.
• Own sourcing strategy and channel economics across inbound, referral, outbound, agency and partner channels; know the cost per hire and quality per channel.
• Own how Sutra.AI is perceived by the candidates we most want to attract, including careers presence, candidate experience and offer-stage conversion.
• Establish a house standard for job descriptions, levelling language and hiring collateral across all functions.
• Close the loop between scorecard and hire quality, and let that evidence reshape how future roles are scoped.
2. Global Team Building & Employment Structure
• Design and run hiring, onboarding and people operations across India and the United States.
• Own contractor-versus-employee decisions, own-entity versus EOR calls, and regional employment contract structures; defend each call commercially.
• Build compensation benchmarking that holds across every market we hire in.
• Establish onboarding that produces productive contributors, not oriented ones, within a defined window.
3. Org Design & Workforce Planning
• Partner with leadership on structure, spans, layers and hiring sequence, anchored to the operating plan rather than to demand.
• Build and maintain a rolling headcount plan tied to revenue and runway.
• Resolve reporting-line and title inconsistencies across the existing organisation and establish a single levelling taxonomy.
• Tell leadership when we are hiring the wrong role at the wrong time, and specify what to hire instead.
4. Performance, Career Frameworks & Total Rewards
• Design career frameworks and competency ladders per function, defining what good looks like at each level.
• Build a performance cycle from first principles that managers and employees find useful, and that makes promotion decisions defensible.
• Own levelling, banding and the annual compensation cycle across both markets, including internal equity management.
• Own ESOP administration and the employee education that makes equity comprehensible.
• Build a recognition programme that rewards behaviour and outcomes rather than tenure.
5. Engagement, Retention & Wellbeing
• Own team health as a measured number: eNPS, pulse surveys, skip-levels and stay interviews.
• Act on what listening mechanisms surface and close the loop visibly.
• Keep regretted attrition low, and diagnose the true cause behind every exit.
• Make working at Sutra.AI feel connected for people who may never share an office.
6. Culture & Internal Communication
• Build the rituals, communication rhythms and feedback loops that make two time zones operate as one company.
• Establish written and verbal communication norms appropriate to a distributed, senior team.
• Keep culture deliberate rather than accidental as headcount grows.
7. People Operations & Compliance
• Own HRIS selection and implementation, policy, payroll coordination and the people data layer.
• Own statutory compliance in India (PF, ESI, POSH, gratuity, S&E, labour codes) and equivalent obligations in the United States and any subsequent geography.
• Build documentation and audit readiness ahead of customer, investor and certification requirements. Our customers operate in healthcare, financial services, aviation and defence-adjacent sectors and will audit our controls.
• Partner with Engineering and Platform on people-side controls relevant to ISO 27001, SOC 2 and equivalent frameworks.
8. Leadership Coaching
• Act as a thought partner to the founders and functional heads on structure, talent and organisational decisions.
• Coach first-time managers into competent ones.
• Have the hard conversations that nobody else in the company is positioned to have, including with leadership.
Focus Areas (Outcomes)
• Hiring: Predictable, forecastable hiring with a defensible quality bar.
• Structure: A levelled, coherent organisation with clear reporting lines and no duplicated accountability.
• Rewards: Compensation that is benchmarked, internally equitable and explainable by managers.
• Retention: Measured team health, low regretted attrition and diagnosed causes.
• Governance: Clean statutory compliance and audit-ready people operations in every geography.
What We're Looking For
Must-Have
• Experience: 15+ years in human resources, including 5+ years owning the function as Head of HR, VP People or CHRO.
• Global Team Building: Demonstrated hiring and people operations across at least two countries; India and the United States preferred.
• Compensation Architecture: Built levelling and compensation frameworks from scratch, not inherited and maintained them.
• Compliance Depth: Fluent in Indian statutory and payroll obligations, with practical working knowledge of US employment requirements.
• Environment: Direct experience in startups or fast-growth technology environments; comfortable operating as the entire function before building a team.
• Talent Market Knowledge: Has hired engineering, data and GTM talent under pressure and understands those markets specifically.
• Stakeholder Management: Proven credibility as a coach and challenger to founders and senior leaders.
Preferred
• Experience scaling an organisation from approximately 50 to 300+ people.
• ESOP design, administration and employee education experience.
• Experience establishing a US entity or EOR arrangement operated from India.
• Exposure to SaaS or AI technology landscapes.
• Experience supporting ISO 27001, SOC 2 or comparable certification from the people-controls side.
This role is NOT for you if
• You need an existing process to run rather than a blank page.
• You view people as downstream of business decisions rather than shaping them.
• You are uncomfortable disagreeing with founders in the room.
• You require permanently remote work. The base location requirement is firm.
Core Competencies
Technical & Functional Competencies
• Talent Acquisition Systems: Scorecard design, structured interviewing, calibration, funnel forecasting and channel economics.
• Organisation Design: Structure, spans and layers, levelling taxonomy, decision rights and workforce planning against an operating plan.
• Total Rewards: Multi-market benchmarking, banding, internal equity, annual cycle design and equity administration.
• Performance Systems: Competency frameworks, review philosophy, promotion governance and manager enablement.
• People Analytics: Attrition, engagement and hiring data used diagnostically, not descriptively.
• Employment Law & Compliance: India statutory obligations, US employment requirements, cross-border employment structures.
• Distributed Team Leadership: Culture, ritual and communication design across time zones.
Behavioural Competencies
• Structural Thinking: Sees duplicated or absent accountability in a messy org and can articulate the fix.
• Candour: Disagrees in the room rather than afterwards, with evidence, and commits fully once decided.
• Data Fluency: Substantiates claims with cohort, manager and period-level evidence.
• Ownership: Operates without oversight and closes problems rather than reporting them.
• Written Clarity: Writes precisely, recognising that in a distributed company unclear writing is unclear thinking at scale.

title: Senior Manager - Founder's Office
description:
We're hiring a Senior Manager – Founder's Office to work directly with the Founder/CEO and the central Centre of Excellence (COE) team at Pepper Content. This role partners closely with our US business and leadership, so you'll be working US hours (5:00 PM – 2:30 AM IST) from our Mumbai office. This is a high-ownership role for someone who thrives in ambiguity, runs hard at problems, and turns founder-level priorities into shipped outcomes. You'll own cross-functional programs spanning AI transformation, GTM, operations, and strategy — and you'll be measured on what gets done, not what gets discussed.
Location & Hours
Base location: Mumbai (in-office).
Working hours: 5:00 PM – 2:30 AM IST, aligned to US business hours, Monday–Friday.
This is non-negotiable — the role requires real-time collaboration with the Founder and US-based stakeholders. Please apply only if you're comfortable with this schedule.
What You'll Do
Drive end-to-end program management for the Founder's most critical initiatives — set goals, define milestones, unblock teams, and ensure on-time, on-quality delivery.
Lead AI transformation programs across the company: identify high-leverage workflows, partner with product/engineering/ops to deploy AI-first solutions, and measure impact on speed, cost, and quality.
Partner with the central COE team to scale playbooks, processes, and tooling across business units — bringing operational rigour to areas that are still founder-led or ad-hoc.
Build dashboards, reviews, and operating cadences (weekly/monthly business reviews, OKR tracking, exec updates) that give the Founder real-time visibility into what's working and what isn't.
Step in as a force multiplier — own special projects end-to-end, from M&A diligence and fundraising prep to new market entry, pricing experiments, or customer escalations.
Translate founder vision into crisp briefs, plans, and execution roadmaps that other teams can run with.
Act as the primary bridge between the India team and US stakeholders — ensuring nothing falls through the cracks across time zones.
What We're Looking For
5–9 years of experience in a mix of consulting (top-tier MBB/Big-4), high-growth startup operations, founder's office, or chief of staff roles.
Demonstrated ability to drive large, cross-functional programs at scale — you've owned things end-to-end, not just coordinated.
Strong bias for action: you default to shipping, not deliberating. You'd rather get a v1 out and iterate than hold a third meeting.
Hands-on familiarity with AI tools (LLMs, agents, automation platforms) and a clear point of view on how AI changes how work gets done. Bonus if you've actually deployed AI workflows in a business setting.
Sharp first-principles thinking, structured problem-solving, and the ability to go from boardroom strategy to spreadsheet-level execution in the same day.
Excellent written and verbal communication — you can write a one-pager that lands with the founder, the board, or a frontline team.
High ownership, low ego, and the operational rigour to follow up on the 100th detail without losing sight of the bigger picture.
Comfortable working US hours from Mumbai on a sustained basis — prior experience working with US teams/clients is a strong plus.
Why This Role
Direct line to the Founder and the leadership team — the work you do shapes company direction.
Front-row seat to AI transformation in a content + marketplace business at scale.
Deep exposure to the US market, which is Pepper's fastest-growing segment.
Fast track to leadership roles within Pepper as the company grows.

title: Program Manager - AI Transformation
description:
MediaMint Combined — MediaMint, DataBeat, and Taktical Digital, 3,000 people across Hyderabad and New York — is
transforming into a Native Agentic company. The Chief Transformation Officer owns the vision, governance, and
execution oversight for AI and agentic adoption across all three companies.
This is a senior program management role. You convert a leadership declaration into a running program: you own the
plan, the operating cadence, the tracking, and the outcomes. You drive every initiative to closure, negotiate with senior
leaders across three companies, and own the single source of truth on transformation progress. When the CTO is with
clients or in the market, you keep the engine running, and you speak with his authority.
We are looking for someone from the media, AdTech, or digital marketing services ecosystem: a program leader who
understands how these businesses run and earns credibility with delivery teams from day one.
This is not a coordination job. It is an ownership job with visible sponsorship from the CEO, COO, and CTO.
What You Will Own
•  Program governance and cadence: run the transformation operating cadence: monthly scorecard, quarterly goal
reviews, and milestone tracking across every initiative and owner.
•  The single view (PMO): own the central registry of every agentic initiative across the three companies: what is being
built, by whom, with what outcome. Leadership should never feel randomized again.
•  Cross-project intelligence and reuse: develop a live perspective on what is working and what is not across every
initiative, and tune accordingly. Build a central repository of skills and reusable assets, keep the best of each
company travelling to the others, and stop teams from building the same thing twice.
•  Benefit realization and measurement: stand up the measurement layer on live solutions. Lock baselines, track
realized benefit against them, and move the program off in-progress and onto reported outcomes.
•  Efficiency goal rollout: drive the 20 to 30 percent delivery efficiency goal into the field: baselines locked,
measurement running, exceptions surfaced, progress reported.
•  Delivery risk and dependency management: own the top program risks to resolution. Manage client dependency as
the leading risk driver, and drive operating-model re-engineering on at-risk solutions where the fix is a way of
working, not just a technical change.
•  Adoption and AI fluency programs: launch and oversee programs like AI Champions, hackathons, and other
initiatives that make AI a natural way of working. Build a base of AI-fluent adopters and influencers, and move
MediaMint toward being genuinely AI native.
•  Leadership communication: prepare board-ready updates, town hall content, and the CTO briefing materials. Draft
first, polish fast, no fluff.
•  Blocker escalation: when an initiative stalls on access, tooling, bandwidth, or a decision, chase it to resolution or
escalate with a recommendation, not a status report.
Who You Are
•  8 to 12 years of experience, with at least 3 in program management, PMO, transformation, strategy, or chief-of-staff
roles in a services, consulting, SaaS, or AdTech environment.
•  Media / AdTech ecosystem background is important: you have worked in or around programmatic, AdOps,
publisher monetization, performance marketing, or media technology, and you understand how these businesses
run. Strong transformation operators from adjacent services worlds will also be considered.
•  You have run programs across multiple senior stakeholders and can hold your own with directors and VPs: push
back, negotiate, and close without needing the sponsor in the room.
•  Real, hands-on AI credibility: you use agentic tools (Claude, ChatGPT, or similar) in your own work weekly and can
demo something you have built or automated. You can sit with builders and judge whether a solution is demo-grade
or production-grade, because you have done the work, not read about it. You will be tested on this.
•  You govern from experience, not theory: you know that anyone can automate the happy path and the value is in
the exceptions, and that an agent should not grade its own work. You can challenge whether a solution can actually
run the business.
•  Structured to a fault: you turn ambiguity into plans, plans into trackers, and trackers into decisions. You measure
what matters and kill vanity metrics.
•  Relationship builder and connector: you build trust across teams and act as the central liaison for AI practice
development and adoption across the group.
•  High ownership, low ego: you are happy for initiative owners to get the credit while you make the whole system
work.
STRONG PLUSES
•  Hands-on experience rolling out AI or agentic programs: copilots, automation platforms, or adoption initiatives.
•  Experience standing up PMO, measurement, or benefit-realization frameworks from scratch.
•  Experience working across India and US teams and time zones.
•  MBA or equivalent: useful, not required. Evidence of shipped outcomes beats credentials.
What Success Looks Like — First 2 Quarters
30 days - Operating cadence live. Central registry and skills repository v1 populated across all three companies.
Efficiency baseline methodology locked with Delivery.
90 days - Scorecard publishing on schedule. Every delivery director has a nominated AI champion. AI Champions
and repository programs running. Measurement layer live on the first set of solutions.
180 days - A stream of agents deployed for internal efficiency, with gains measured against baseline. Agentic
governance framework developed and adopted. AI Champions and central repository programs
running successfully, with duplicate builds cut and reuse visible across projects. POC to production
conversion tracked. The CTO is spending measurably less time on program mechanics and more on
strategy and clients.
WHY THIS ROLE
•  Rare vantage point: you see and shape the AI transformation of an entire 3,000-person group, three companies and
ten countries, from the sponsor's seat.
•  Direct exposure to the CEO, COO, and the leadership of all three companies from week one.
•  The transformation is funded, sponsored, and declared. You are not selling the idea internally; you are making it real.
•  Clear growth path: this role is designed to grow into a transformation or business leadership position as the program
scales.
Information Security & ISO 27001 Compliance
Security is at the heart of everything we do. In this role, you will be strictly required to uphold our Information Security Management System (ISMS) policies in alignment with ISO/IEC 27001 standards. Responsibilities include safeguarding sensitive asset data, completing mandatory security awareness training, reporting potential security incidents or vulnerabilities immediately, and ensuring that daily operations comply with our rigorous data protection protocols.

title: Strategy Manager, Founder's Office
description:
Strategy Manager, Founder's Office
Location: New Delhi, India
Experience: 2-5 years
About the Company
We are building an AI-powered personal finance platform designed to help people make smarter decisions with their money. The company brings together technology, financial insight, and practical decision support to address a real and recurring need: helping users understand their choices and act with greater confidence. As the business grows, the Founder’s Office plays a central role in converting important questions into clear priorities, rigorous plans, and measurable outcomes. This is an opportunity to contribute close to the company’s most consequential decisions while working across functions and problem areas. The Strategy Manager will help strengthen the operating cadence behind a mission-led financial technology business, connecting analysis with execution and ensuring that strategic intent translates into progress. You will work in an environment where the quality of thinking, speed of learning, and ability to align teams directly influence how effectively the platform serves its users and builds durable business momentum.
About the Role
As Strategy Manager in the Founder’s Office, you will own high-priority strategic workstreams from problem definition through execution and measurable business impact. You will partner with the Founder and senior leaders to structure ambiguous questions, develop decision-ready analysis, and turn conclusions into coordinated action. The role combines business strategy, operating problem-solving, and cross-functional program leadership. Success means creating clarity where priorities compete, moving important initiatives forward, and building the systems, metrics, and follow-through needed to sustain results. You will work across the organization, connect teams around shared outcomes, and surface risks before they slow execution. This role is suited to an operator who can move comfortably between detailed analysis and senior-level communication, and who is motivated by the opportunity to shape a growing AI-powered personal finance platform.
Key Responsibilities
• Own strategic initiatives sponsored by the Founder, defining objectives, milestones, decision rights, and success metrics so complex priorities translate into accountable execution and measurable business outcomes.
• Structure ambiguous business questions through market, customer, financial, and operational analysis, producing concise recommendations that improve the quality and speed of leadership decisions.
• Build operating mechanisms for priority initiatives, including review cadences, dashboards, issue logs, and escalation paths that keep cross-functional teams aligned and expose delivery risks early.
• Partner with functional leaders to translate strategy into executable plans, resolve dependencies, and maintain momentum across initiatives spanning product, growth, operations, finance, and technology.
• Prepare leadership materials, investment cases, and performance updates that connect evidence, trade-offs, and actions, enabling the Founder and senior team to make informed choices.
• Track initiative performance against agreed outcomes, diagnose variance, and recommend course corrections that protect business impact rather than merely reporting activity.
• Identify repeatable processes and decision frameworks that improve organizational leverage, institutionalize learning, and help the company scale its execution discipline.
Essential Skills & Technologies
• Strong problem structuring, quantitative analysis, and business judgment, with the ability to move from incomplete information to clear recommendations and practical execution plans.
• Proven cross-functional program leadership and stakeholder management, including the ability to create alignment, manage dependencies, and influence senior decision-makers without relying on formal authority.
• Excellent written and verbal communication, with experience developing executive narratives, operating reviews, financial analyses, and decision materials that make complex issues easy to act upon.
• Advanced proficiency with spreadsheets and presentation tools; comfort working with data, dashboards, and analytical systems to monitor performance and support fact-based decisions.
• Working understanding of digital products, technology businesses, or financial services, with curiosity about how AI can improve personal financial decision-making.
Additional Plus
• Experience in a strategy, consulting, business operations, investment banking, venture capital, or Founder’s Office role within a high-growth company.
• Exposure to consumer fintech, personal finance, AI-enabled products, or regulated financial services, with an ability to connect user needs to commercial and operating outcomes.
• Experience building planning processes, management dashboards, or cross-functional operating rhythms that have improved execution quality at scale.
What You'll Bring
• You bring at least 2 years of experience in strategy, consulting, business operations, finance, product strategy, or a similarly analytical and execution-oriented role. Exceptional candidates with less experience will also be considered when they demonstrate unusual ownership, structured thinking, and the ability to deliver meaningful outcomes.
• You are comfortable taking ownership of an undefined problem, decomposing it into a clear structure, and driving the work toward a decision or outcome. You combine analytical depth with commercial judgment: you know when more analysis is needed and when the organization needs a clear recommendation and decisive action.
• You can work directly with founders and senior leaders while remaining effective with functional teams responsible for delivery. You communicate with precision, write clearly, and tailor your message to the audience, whether presenting a concise leadership recommendation or aligning a team around next steps.
• You are highly organized, reliable with follow-through, and able to manage several priorities without losing sight of impact. You bring intellectual curiosity about AI, technology, and personal finance, along with the humility to learn quickly.
• Most importantly, you are motivated by ownership: you measure your effectiveness by the decisions improved, initiatives advanced, and business outcomes delivered.
Why Join Us
• Work directly with the Founder on high-priority questions that shape the direction, operating model, and growth of an AI-powered personal finance platform.
• Gain broad exposure across strategy, product, finance, operations, and technology while owning work that connects senior-level decisions to measurable execution outcomes.
• Help build a company focused on enabling people to make smarter decisions with their money, applying rigorous thinking to a meaningful and practical user problem.
What We Offer
• A high-ownership role in the Founder’s Office, with the opportunity to define important problems, shape recommendations, and see strategic decisions carried through to implementation.
• Direct exposure to the operating challenges of an AI-powered personal finance platform, with meaningful cross-functional scope across business and execution priorities.
• An on-site opportunity in New Delhi for a strategy operator who wants to combine analytical work, senior stakeholder partnership, and hands-on delivery.

title: Chief of Staff
description:
About E2M
E2M is a leading white-label growth partner for digital agencies worldwide, helping them scale through expert web development, digital marketing, and AI-powered solutions.
With 13+ years of experience, 350+ professionals, and 400+ agency partners globally, E2M offers services across WordPress, Shopify, SEO, PPC, content marketing, and AI automation.
Driven by an agency-first approach and our Black Label Standard, we work as an extension of our partners' teams, delivering quality, innovation, and reliable digital solutions that help them grow.
Role Purpose
We are looking for an exceptional Chief of Staff / Executive Operator to work directly with our CEO across multiple businesses and strategic initiatives.
This is not a traditional administrative or project management role. We need a highly proactive, resourceful operator who can take ideas, priorities, and problems and turn them into completed outcomes with minimal oversight.
You will serve as an extension of the CEO, helping drive execution, eliminate operational friction, and ensure important commitments don't get lost between meetings, teams, and business units.
The ideal candidate is a builder and problem-solver who thrives in ambiguity, embraces technology and AI, and takes pride in making things happen.
Your mission: Make sure more important things get done without the CEO having to manage them.
Location: Ahmedabad, India (Hybrid / Office-Based)
Reports To: Group CEO
Schedule: Full-time, with regular overlap with US Mountain Time
Key Responsibilities
1. Executive Operations & CEO Leverage
• Own and maintain a centralized system for tracking the CEO's priorities, commitments, follow-ups, and outstanding decisions.
• Proactively manage executive workflows, meeting preparation, communications, and follow-through.
• Prepare concise daily executive briefings highlighting priorities, decisions, deadlines, and potential issues.
• Identify work that can be eliminated, delegated, automated, or independently completed.
• Protect the CEO's time by minimizing unnecessary meetings, interruptions, and administrative activities.
• Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to move work forward without requiring constant direction.
2. Independent Project Execution
• Take ambiguous ideas and business objectives and independently turn them into actionable projects and completed deliverables.

• Anticipate roadblocks, solve problems, and proactively maintain momentum.

3. Process Improvement, AI & Automation
• Identify repetitive tasks, operational bottlenecks, and inefficient workflows.
• Design and implement simple, practical solutions that reduce manual work and complexity.
• Leverage AI tools, agents, and automations to improve the CEO's effectiveness.

4. Leadership Accountability & Business Execution
• Support Weekly Business Reviews (WBRs), Monthly Business Reviews (MBRs), and executive operating rhythms.

• Proactively follow up with stakeholders, identify delays, and help remove blockers.

• Support growth initiatives, strategic partnerships, business development, and special projects.

• Represent the CEO's priorities in appropriate internal discussions.
• Build effective working relationships with leadership teams in India and North America.
• Exercise sound judgment, discretion, and appropriate decision-making authority.
Outcomes & Measures of Success
Success in this role will be measured primarily by outcomes, not activity.
CEO Leverage
• Measurable reduction in time spent by the CEO on administrative work, coordination, and follow-up.
• Reliable visibility into priorities, commitments, and pending decisions.
• Fewer operational issues requiring direct CEO involvement.
Independent Execution
• Multiple important initiatives completed with limited CEO intervention.
• Consistent follow-through on commitments and deadlines.
• Demonstrated ability to move projects forward without waiting for direction.
Operational Improvement
• Recurring workflows simplified, automated, or eliminated.
• Tangible reductions in manual effort and operational friction.
• Practical solutions that are adopted and maintained without unnecessary bureaucracy.
Leadership Effectiveness
• Critical commitments consistently tracked and completed.
• Clear, concise executive briefings and business updates.
• Strong coordination across teams without duplicating existing leadership responsibilities.
Required Competencies
Extreme Ownership: Takes responsibility for results and sees things through to completion.
Proactive Execution: Identifies what needs to happen and acts without waiting for instructions.
Bias for Action: Prefers implementing a practical solution over prolonged analysis or planning.
Resourcefulness: Can independently research, troubleshoot, build, and solve unfamiliar problems.
Simplification: Naturally looks for ways to eliminate complexity and unnecessary work.
Business Judgment: Understands priorities, makes thoughtful decisions, and knows when to escalate.
Exceptional Follow-Through: Nothing important gets lost, forgotten, or left unresolved.
AI & Technical Fluency: Actively uses AI, automation, and productivity tools to increase efficiency and execution capacity.
Executive Communication: Communicates clearly and concisely with senior stakeholders, particularly in a distributed international environment.
Adaptability: Comfortable switching between tactical execution and strategic initiatives.
Ideal Candidate Profile
• 5+ years of relevant experience in business operations, executive operations, project execution, entrepreneurship, or a Chief of Staff capacity.
• Demonstrated experience independently delivering business projects and solving operational problems.
• Strong written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate effectively with US-based executives.
• Experience working with international teams, preferably US-based organizations.
• High proficiency with Google Workspace, Slack, and modern productivity tools.
• Hands-on experience using AI tools such as ChatGPT or Claude.
• Familiarity with workflow automation platforms such as Zapier or n8n is highly desirable.
• Strong analytical skills and financial/business literacy.
• High discretion and comfort handling confidential business information.
• Comfortable working with regular US Mountain Time overlap.
Previous experience as a founder, operations leader, senior executive assistant, or Chief of Staff is valuable, but demonstrated independent execution is more important than job title.
How We Work
We value people who take initiative, solve problems, and deliver results.
Our operating principles for this role are straightforward:
• Own the outcome, not just the task.
• Solve problems before escalating them.
• Build the solution instead of just documenting the problem.
• Keep things simple.
• Close the loop on every commitment.
• Protect the CEO's time and attention.
• Move forward without waiting for perfect instructions.
This role requires someone who is comfortable with ambiguity, trusted to make decisions within established boundaries, and energized by turning complex business challenges into simple, completed solutions.
We are looking for a doer who thinks, not a thinker who occasionally does.

title: Chief of Staff
description:
About Us
Chief of Staff to the CEO
Summary
This senior, full-time individual contributor role serves as a strategic partner to the Chief Executive Officer, operating from Pune with occasional travel to Singapore and key market locations. Designed as a two-to-three-year engagement, the position offers company-wide visibility, collaborating closely with five Product Business Unit (PBU) heads, the CTO organization, and cross-functional leaders in delivery, marketing, finance, and talent. The primary purpose of this role is to establish and maintain a robust operating system that enables the CEO to focus on high-level strategy, capital allocation, and critical personnel decisions. By managing the rhythm of the organization and ensuring seamless execution of cross-unit commitments, the Chief of Staff empowers PBU leaders to drive their respective units effectively while the CEO maintains direct oversight without being bottlenecked by coordination tasks.
Responsibilities
• Orchestrate Operating Rhythms: Manage the end-to-end monthly portfolio review, including agenda setting, standardizing pre-reads, tracking decision logs, and ensuring action items are assigned and completed.
• Develop Outcome Metrics: Create and maintain a unified scorecard for each PBU focusing on business impact, customer satisfaction, and product reliability, collaborating with Finance and Product Marketing to validate data sources.
• Manage Cross-Unit Dependencies: Maintain a central register of customer commitments and shared roadmap items, proactively identifying and resolving conflicts before they impact delivery or client relationships.
• Streamline Executive Decision-Making: Triage and frame all requests requiring CEO attention with clear facts, options, and recommendations, ensuring rapid turnaround times and documenting final decisions for accountability.
• Drive Transformation Execution: Track the implementation of the new PBU operating model, including organizational changes and interim reporting, and prepare strategic reviews with data-driven recommendations for future structural adjustments.
• Facilitate Leadership Alignment: Run the weekly leadership cadence, quarterly business reviews, and annual planning cycles, ensuring high standards for pre-reads, minutes, and action tracking across all forums.
• Monitor Strategic Progress: Partner with the CFO to track company-wide objectives regarding growth, profitability, AI deployment, and market expansion, providing concise monthly updates to the CEO and leadership team.
• Prepare Board and Shareholder Materials: Oversee the quality and timeline of board packs and shareholder reports, ensuring consistency and accuracy in all content derived from functional teams.
• Lead Special Initiatives: Manage time-bound projects scoped by the CEO, such as revenue team reorganizations, new market entry groundwork, and AI strategy rollout, ensuring clear scope, deadlines, and handovers.
• Draft Executive Communications: Author decision memos, briefing notes, and internal communications for the CEO, collaborating with the Content team to ensure external messaging accurately reflects facts and decisions.
• Maintain Local Presence: Act as the daily representative of the CEO office in Pune, providing early insights into unit operations and delivering candid, necessary information to leadership.
Requirements
Requirements:
• Education: An MBA from a top-tier business school (such as an IIM) is required; an undergraduate degree in engineering or a quantitative field is highly preferred.
• Experience: Eight to twelve years of professional experience, including at least three years in a top-tier management consulting firm with a track record of managing engagement managers or equivalent workstreams for C-suite clients.
• Industry Background: Minimum of two years of operational experience within a software, SaaS, or technology product company, specifically in strategy, operations, program management, or a Chief of Staff capacity.
• Proven Track Record: Demonstrated success in leading cross-functional programs to completion within organizations of 200 to 500 employees, with a focus on delivering tangible outcomes rather than just plans.
• Board-Level Competence: Experience in preparing and presenting materials for board-level audiences and working directly with engineering and product leaders to understand the software development lifecycle.
• Core Skills: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, the ability to analyze financial data independently, proficiency in running meetings that result in clear decisions, and the capability to build data-driven scorecards from raw inputs.
• Technical Fluency: Comfortable integrating AI tools into daily workflows and expects similar adoption across teams.
• Working Style: A low-ego professional with a strong commitment to follow-through, capable of delivering difficult truths to senior leadership, and dedicated to seeing problems through to resolution without seeking public credit.
• Location: Must be based in Pune or willing to relocate prior to commencement, with the ability to travel occasionally to Singapore.
Benefits Why Join Anchanto
At Anchanto, we believe in creating an environment where people can build meaningful careers, continuously develop their capabilities and gain exposure to a truly global business.
• Global Exposure: Work with diverse teams, customers and stakeholders across international markets and gain experience in a global B2B SaaS environment.
• Learning & Development: We invest in our people through sponsored learning, certifications and development opportunities aligned with your professional growth.
• International & Onsite Opportunities: Client-facing roles may offer opportunities to travel and work onsite with customers across our global markets.
• Medical Insurance: Comprehensive medical insurance coverage to support you & your family's health and well-being.
• Comprehensive Leave Benefits: Maternity, Paternity, Marriage and Bereavement leave, along with Comp Off and flexibility to support important personal commitments.
• Recognition for Long-Term Contribution: Tenured employees are eligible for additional monetary benefits, extra paid leave and company-sponsored paid vacations as part of our commitment to recognising long-term contribution.
• Flexibility & Work-Life Balance: A supportive and flexible work environment that enables employees to manage professional responsibilities alongside personal priorities.
• Meaningful Career Growth: Take ownership of challenging, high-impact work and contribute to products and solutions that serve global brands, retailers and logistics businesses.

title: Associate Director/Director - GenAI Business Strategy & Transformation
company: D. E. Shaw India Private Limited
description:
The D. E. Shaw group is a global investment and technology development firm with more than $115 billion in investment capital as of September 1, 2026, and offices in North America, Europe, and Asia. Since our founding in 1988, our firm has earned an international reputation for successful investing based on innovation, careful risk management, and the quality and depth of our staff. We have a significant presence in the world's capital markets, investing in a wide range of companies and financial instruments in both developed and developing economies.
We are looking for a GenAI Business Strategy & Transformation Lead to anchor the DESIS GenAI-for-Business ("GAIBiz") effort. Depending on the candidate’s location preference, the position is open for either of our Hyderabad, Bengaluru, or Gurugram offices in India. This person will be responsible for translating the firm's GenAI strategy into tangible adoption and measurable outcomes across the DESIS environment, working in close partnership with the strategy and transformation core based in the firm's global offices. This is a role largely built around execution and adoption. The strategy setting and transformation agenda is driven centrally; the mandate here is to land that agenda well within DESIS, shaping it for the local context, driving uptake, and delivering results on the ground. There will be real opportunities to influence direction and expand scope over time, but a candidate who thrives will be one who is energized by making things happen, not solely by setting up the agenda. This role will offer a good mix of strategy formulation and hands on delivery experience, tilting more towards later.
WHAT YOU'LL DO DAY-TO-DAY:
In this role, you will drive GenAI adoption across DESIS by moving initiatives from pilot to production use; conceptualizing and executing novel ways to increase adoption; and owning the associated logistics and change-management scaffolding (enablement, incentives, communications, feedback loops) needed to turn well-designed programs into genuine, sustained uptake. You will partner with the global strategy and transformation core, acting as the DESIS anchor for firmwide GenAI strategy, ensuring initiatives are contextualized, sequenced, and executed effectively in and for the DESIS environment. You will engage credibly with technical teams, working shoulder to shoulder with engineering and data teams, understanding architecture, model capabilities, and tradeoffs well enough to challenge, prioritize, and unblock. You will embed risk, compliance, and data governance, ensuring GenAI initiatives meet the firm's standards for data protection, model risk, regulatory expectations, and responsible-AI practice from the outset, not as an afterthought. Finally, you will measure and communicate impact by defining the metrics that matter, tracking adoption and value realization, and reporting progress clearly to senior stakeholders across DESIS and the global firm.
WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR:
The ideal candidate should hold-
Basic qualifications:
• 15 or more years of experience in leading GenAI and tech transformation
• Sound instincts on when to buy, when to build, and when a middle path serves best, with the commercial sense to weigh cost, speed, and control (Strategic and commercial judgment)
• A demonstrated track record of driving uptake, not just designing programs. Evidence of moving organizations from intent to embedded behavior (Change management and adoption)
• Deep enough understanding of GenAI and modern data/ML systems to engage engineers credibly and make informed trade-offs. You need not be a builder, but you must be conversant (Technical literacy)
• Experience in or adjacent to market finance, hedge funds, or investment management, with enough fluency to earn the trust of demanding stakeholders (Domain credibility)
• Practical familiarity with the risk, regulatory, and data-governance considerations that shape how AI can responsibly be deployed in a financial-services setting (Risk, compliance and data governance)
• Pragmatic and outcome-obsessed approach, with a high tolerance for ambiguity and rapid change. Ability to influence without authority across a distributed, matrixed organization, and comfort in operating primarily in a delivery-focused capacity within a globally driven agenda (Temperament and influencing skills)

Their AI agents run 50 lakh+ calls a day for 60+ leading brands including Kotak Mahindra Bank, AngelOne, PhonePe, IndiaMART, TATA Digital, Amazon, Swiggy and Eureka Forbes, giving every lead the best pitch, in their language, on their preferred channel, at the right time. Developed by them, the world's first Sales LLM, is trained on 400M+ real sales interactions and their outcomes, so it learns what actually closes, not just what sounds fluent. We process over a trillion tokens a month at under 0.8 second median latency, and every conversation makes the next one better. Driven by 200+ builders and backed by Blume Ventures, Chiratae Ventures and Bertelsmann India Investments, we believe how we build matters as much as what we build. Ownership is real, trust is the default, and there is room for deep work. Careers here are not one-size-fits-all. title: Chief of Staff (Founder's office)
description:
Chief of Staff to the CEO
Role: Chief of Staff to the CEO
Department: CEO Office
Reports To: CEO
Location: Gurugram
Work timings: 3pm IST to 12am+ (Half US overlapping hours)
Team Stage: Series B
Team: Leads the CEO Office (Program & Strategy Managers, Founder's Office Associates)
Key Partners: CEO, Executive Team, Board & Investors, Product, Engineering, GTM, Customer Success, Finance, People
About Spyne
Spyne is building the AI operating system for automotive retail. It started with visual merchandising and has expanded into conversational AI. Spyne helps dealers move inventory faster, respond to buyers instantly, and run more of the dealership stack with AI. Founded by operators from Amazon, Cox, and OYO, Spyne has grown 30x in under three years and now powers 1,500+ dealerships across the US. Its products, Studio AI and Vini AI, are coming together into a full-stack Retail AI platform for modern dealerships.
• Rooftops live: 2,000+
• Growth: 2.5 to 3x a year for 3 consecutive years
• Revenue from the US: 80%+
• Net revenue retention: above 110%
• Integrations: 70+ across CRM, DMS, inventory, service and finance
• Team: 200+, primarily India-based
• Capital raised: $25M+ from Accel, Vertex Ventures and Storm Ventures
Why This Role Exists
Spyne is scaling faster than its operating system can keep up. The CEO's time is the company's scarcest resource. It is split across fundraising, US dealer groups, product bets and a fast-growing leadership team. We need a Chief of Staff who extends the CEO's reach. That means someone who runs how the company makes decisions, sets priorities and follows through, so the CEO can spend their time on the few things only a CEO can do.
This is not an executive assistant role, and it is not a pure strategy role. You will be the CEO's thought partner and the company's operating backbone. You will own the leadership cadence, drive the most important cross-functional bets from start to finish, and lead the CEO Office team. On many issues you will speak for the CEO, so the leadership team and the board must trust your judgment.
In the last 6 months, this seat would have meant:
• Designing and running the company's operating rhythm: annual and quarterly planning, OKRs, weekly exec staff and monthly business reviews across every function
• Owning board meeting preparation from start to finish: the board deck, pre-reads, metric definitions, and follow-through on board asks
• Leading the fundraising workstream alongside the CEO: the investor narrative, the data room, diligence management and investor updates
• Building the business case and 12-week launch plan for a new product line, covering pricing, pilot selection, vendor contracts and the handoff to a GM
• Designing the ESOP distribution framework across ~200 employees and working through leveling and compensation questions with People and Finance
• Running the org design and senior hiring process for new leadership roles, from role scoping to closing candidates
• Framing M&A-adjacent and partnership questions (build vs. buy vs. partner) deeply enough for a CEO decision
• Running competitive research deep enough to reposition a product against incumbents
• Prototyping internal tools with Claude Code or Cursor, such as leadership dashboards and planning trackers, instead of writing a spec and waiting
Some weeks you're in spreadsheets pressure-testing unit economics before a board meeting. Some weeks you're on calls with US dealer groups or investors. Some weeks you're sorting out a stuck decision between two exec team members. Some weeks you're shipping a v0 of something yourself because that's faster than briefing a team.
What You'll Do
• Be the CEO's force multiplier. Triage what reaches the CEO, prepare them for high-stakes meetings, and make sure every decision they make has an owner, a deadline and follow-through. Represent the CEO in forums they can't attend, and make calls on their behalf within agreed limits.
• Own the company operating system. Run annual and quarterly planning, OKRs, exec staff meetings, business reviews and the leadership offsite. Define the metrics the company runs on and keep one version of the truth across Finance, GTM and Product.
• Drive exec team alignment. Spot misaligned priorities between functions early. Sales, Product, CS and Finance often optimize for different things, and most failures happen at the handoffs between them. Bring disagreements to a decision instead of letting them drag on.
• Run board and investor work. Own board meeting preparation, board materials and investor updates. Co-lead fundraising with the CEO and Finance: the narrative, the model, the data room and diligence.
• Lead the company's highest-priority initiatives. A new SKU launch touches product, legal, sales and data partnerships. You own the outcome, find the blocking dependency early, and hand it to a permanent owner once it runs on its own.
• Do the analysis behind big decisions. Market sizing, pricing models, build-vs-buy calls, M&A screens, org design. Your output goes straight to the CEO and often to the board, so it has to be right and it has to be readable.
• Shape the organization. Partner with People on org design, senior hiring, leveling, ESOPs and leadership onboarding. Help the company grow the leadership bench it needs for its next stage.
• Own internal and executive communication. Draft or shape all-hands content, CEO memos, strategy docs and company-wide announcements, so that 200+ people across India and the US understand the priorities and the reasons behind them.
• Build and lead the CEO Office. Hire, manage and develop the Program & Strategy Managers and Founder's Office Associates. Decide which problems the office takes on, and graduate its projects into the business.
• Build with AI tools. Spyne sells AI software and runs on it internally. Set the standard for how the leadership team uses AI, from automated reporting to prototyping internal tools in a weekend.
Who does well here
• 6–10 years of experience, including a mix of top consulting (MBB or equivalent, ideally at Engagement Manager level or above) and operating roles in a high-growth startup: Chief of Staff, Founder's Office, BizOps, or leading a function
• A track record of operating at the executive level. You have run a planning cycle, prepared board materials, or managed a leadership team's operating cadence
• Evidence you've shipped something end to end, not just advised on it: a product, an internal tool, a new function, a launch
• You have managed people and can lead a small, high-output team
• The judgment and discretion to handle confidential information on fundraising, compensation, people and M&A
• The executive presence to earn the trust of the leadership team and push back on them, including the CEO
• Genuinely fluent with AI tools. You'll be asked in the interview what you've built with them
• Strong with numbers. You can build a model from scratch and defend every assumption in it in front of a board
• Exposure to B2B SaaS, US markets, or automotive retail is a plus, not a requirement
• Comfortable with ambiguity and speed. Priorities shift weekly; you'd rather have that than a roadmap
• Willing to work India hours that overlap with US time zones, since customers, investors and many counterparties are in the US
Why this seat
You'll be a direct partner to the CEO across every part of a Series B company: the board, fundraising, pricing, hiring, product strategy, M&A and org design. This seat sees the whole company, and the highest-leverage problems land here first. People who do this well typically go on to run a business unit, a major function, or company-wide strategy as Spyne scales.

title: Director of AI Labs Business Unit
description:
🚀 About Joveo
Joveo builds AI-powered recruiting technology. We are building a team to deliver specialist human data and AI evaluation programs, with expert judgment at the centre of the work.
We are hiring a director to shape this capability and build the organisation that delivers it.
🌟 About the role
Build the function that turns specialist human expertise into AI data and evaluations customers can rely on.
You will work with Joveo leadership to shape the offering, hire the managers who deliver it and establish the standards we commit to. Your remit includes customer delivery and portfolio economics, with influence over the tools and capabilities we develop.
For someone who has already led complex AI programs, this is an opportunity to put that experience to work across an entire function. You will help decide which opportunities we pursue, what a successful pilot must demonstrate and how we grow without losing control of quality or cost.
🧠 What you’ll do
• Shape the offering with leadership. Identify the customer problems we can solve well, define the deliverables and acceptance standards, and establish what we need to prove before expanding a service.
• Build the delivery leadership team. Hire and develop program managers and specialist leads. Give them clear accountability and decision rights, and plan expert capacity around qualified demand.
• Establish quality standards across programs. Set expectations for expert qualification, calibration, adjudication and measurement. Work with technical specialists to challenge weak metrics and keep evaluation conclusions defensible.
• Lead senior customer conversations. Translate technical needs into realistic commitments, resolve difficult escalations and use customer feedback to improve the offering. Help turn successful pilots into repeat programs.
• Own delivery economics across the portfolio. Understand the full cost of expert supply, technical integration and rework. Partner with commercial teams on pricing, scope changes and capacity decisions.
• Shape tooling priorities with engineering. Turn recurring delivery problems into reusable capabilities, make deliberate choices about automation and maintain strong practices for customer data protection and traceability.
🎯 What we’re looking for
• You have built or led a delivery, operations or technical program function in AI data, evaluation, applied AI or a closely related field.
• You have hired or developed managers and held responsibility for complex customer outcomes. You can build a team that makes good decisions without every issue reaching you.
• You are credible in both a technical review and a commercial discussion. You can challenge an evaluation design, identify weak acceptance criteria and work through the implications for delivery and cost.
• You have made consequential operating decisions: narrowing an offering, resetting a customer commitment, changing a quality system or rebuilding a team. You can explain your reasoning and the results.
• Experience launching a service, turning pilots into repeat programs or operating expert contributor networks is especially relevant.
We will look at the scope you have carried and the judgment you have developed. Your record of building a function matters more than the title you currently hold.
✨ Why join Joveo
You will help shape this capability while its operating choices are still taking form. Your decisions will influence the work we pursue, the leaders we hire and the standards customers experience.
This role brings technical delivery and commercial responsibility together. If you have strong convictions about how complex AI programs should run, you will have the scope to build an organisation around them.
